# yabbistir extensions: the full documentation

Every document llms.txt lists, in its order, in one file. Generated by `npm run docs`; links between documents are relative to the repository's root folder or to the document's own folder.


================================================================================
File: AGENTS.md
================================================================================

# AGENTS.md

You are working in the store repository for yabbistir extensions. yabbistir is a clipboard history app for macOS. An extension is a folder with a `manifest.json`, TypeScript in `src/`, strings in `locales/`, and tests. The build bundles `src/index.ts` into one `index.js` that runs in **JavaScriptCore, not Node**, inside yabbistir's helper process. The extension only computes and returns data; **the app draws all UI**.

Every coding agent works from this file; `CLAUDE.md` only imports it (`@AGENTS.md`). Everything you need is in this file and in `docs/`. Read [docs/getting-started.md](docs/getting-started.md) once, then [docs/concepts.md](docs/concepts.md), and look things up in [docs/manifest.md](docs/manifest.md), [docs/api.md](docs/api.md) and [docs/errors.md](docs/errors.md). Do not guess an API or a manifest field: both references are generated from the code.

## Repository map

```text
extensions/<id>/             one extension per folder; <id> is its reverse-domain id
  manifest.json              what it is, its permissions, what it contributes
  src/index.ts               exports actions, detectors and/or captureRules
  locales/en.json            English strings (required); locales/tr.json optional
  tests/*.test.mjs           node:test tests against the fake host
  README.md, CHANGELOG.md    required
  icon.png                   optional; most use an SF Symbol ("sf:<name>") instead
templates/<kind>/            what `npm run new` copies: action, detector, capture-rule, job
packages/api/index.d.ts      the API's types, @yabbistir/api (copied from the app; do not edit)
packages/api/fake-host.mjs   createFakeHost() for tests (its header lists every option)
schema/                      manifest.schema.json (copied from the app; do not edit), catalog.schema.json
tools/                       new, dev, validate, test, build, docs, catalog, sign, pr-checks; tools/test holds their tests
docs/                        guides; manifest.md and api.md are generated by `npm run docs`
docs/recipes/                six complete example extensions
dist/                        build output (ignored by git)
llms.txt, llms-full.txt      the docs' index, and all docs in one file (generated)
```

Real extensions to learn from: `dev.yabbistir.video-download` (job, exec, network, variants, file result), `dev.yabbistir.link-clean` (capture rule), `dev.yabbistir.jwt` (detector and preview), `dev.yabbistir.translate` (variants, AI, translation).

## Commands

Run every command from the repository's root. Node 24 (22.18 or later works); run `npm install` once.

| Command | When |
|---|---|
| `npm run new -- <id> --template <action\|detector\|capture-rule\|job> [--author <name>]` | To start an extension. Creates `extensions/<id>/`, which passes validate and test at once. `author` is how you want to be credited, your name or your GitHub user name; without `--author` it comes from `git config user.name`, and the output says so. |
| `npm test -- <id>` | After every change to `src/` or `tests/`. Add `--test-name-pattern=<name>` for one test. |
| `npm run validate -- <id>` | After every change to `manifest.json` or `locales/`. Prints file, field, problem and fix per line; exit 1 on errors. With a build newer than the source it checks that build too, `index.js` included; otherwise it notes "not built yet (or out of date)". |
| `npm run build -- <id>` | Before you finish. Bundles into `dist/<id>/`, validates that folder, writes `dist/<id>-<version>.yabext`. Catches Node imports. |
| `npm run typecheck` | Before you finish: TypeScript over every extension's `src/`. |
| `npm run dev -- <id>` | To try it in the app: links `dist/<id>` into `~/Library/Application Support/yabbistir/Extensions/` and rebuilds on change. Long-running; `--once` builds and links without watching. Only when a person asks you to, on their Mac. |
| `npm run docs` | Only when you changed `docs/`, `llms.txt`, the schema or `packages/api`: regenerates `docs/manifest.md`, `docs/api.md` and `llms-full.txt`. Commit the result. |
| `npm run test:tools` | Only when you changed `tools/`, `templates/`, `packages/` or `docs/`. |
| `npm run pr-checks` | Before you open a pull request, with the change committed: every check the pull request gets ([Publishing](docs/publishing.md#the-checks)), for the commits since `origin/main`. Takes a few minutes. |

## Rules

1. **Change only your own extension's folder**, `extensions/<id>/`. One extension per pull request. Do not edit `tools/`, `templates/`, `packages/`, `schema/` or another extension unless that is the task itself, in a separate change.
2. **No Node.** No `fs`, `path`, `child_process`, `http`, `crypto` (Node's), `events`, `util`, `url`, `buffer` imports (not even npm packages with those names), and no `process`, `Buffer`, `require`, `global`, `__dirname`. Use the `yab` API and web standards: `URL`, `TextEncoder`, `TextDecoder`, `atob`, `btoa`, `fetch`, `setTimeout`, `AbortController`, `crypto.randomUUID`, `Intl`. See [docs/errors.md#node-builtins](docs/errors.md#node-builtins). (Tests run in Node and may use `node:` modules; only `src/` runs in the app.)
3. **Fewest permissions.** None is the default and enough for most extensions. Add `network` (with `network.domains`), `exec` (with `requires.tools`), `capture` or `history` only when the extension cannot work without it, and say why in the README. On-device AI, translation, images and files in the work folder need no permission. See [docs/permissions.md](docs/permissions.md).
4. **English is required.** Every key the manifest uses is in `locales/en.json`. Every text a person reads is a locale key in the manifest and goes through `yab.t` in code. Other languages are optional.
5. **Extensions never draw UI.** Return results, tags, preview sections, progress and messages; the app draws them in its calm grey look. No colors, no emoji decoration, no HTML layouts. See [docs/design-guidelines.md](docs/design-guidelines.md).
6. **`exec` arguments are fixed or checked.** Item content goes after `--`; no shell; no options that run other programs.
7. **No data leaves the Mac** except what the action is for, when the person runs it. Never log the item's content or a secret.

## Definition of done

- In this order: `npm test -- <id>` passes; `npm run build -- <id>` passes; then `npm run validate -- <id>` reports no errors and no warnings and ends with `extensions/<id>: ok, with its build in dist/<id>`; and `npm run typecheck` is clean. Validate's "not built yet (or out of date)" note is not a warning: it means validate could not check `index.js`, and building first, then validating, makes it go away.
- Tests cover the main path, each message a person can see, and the expected failures (empty input, missing tool, failed request, cancel).
- `README.md` says what the extension does, gives an example, and explains every permission and tool. `CHANGELOG.md` has a `## <version>` section for the manifest's `version`.
- A change to an existing extension raises its `version` and adds a CHANGELOG section.
- Only `extensions/<id>/` changed (plus the root `package-lock.json` if you added a library).

## The essentials

A transform action, complete. The manifest's text fields are **keys** into the locale files:

```json
{
  "id": "dev.yourname.upper",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "apiVersion": 1,
  "defaultLocale": "en",
  "name": "name",
  "description": "description",
  "icon": "sf:textformat",
  "author": "your-github-name",
  "license": "MIT",
  "categories": ["text"],
  "contributes": {
    "actions": [
      { "id": "upper", "title": "upper.title", "keywords": "upper.keywords", "input": "item",
        "accepts": { "kinds": ["text", "code"] }, "output": "text" }
    ]
  }
}
```

```json
{
  "name": "Upper Case",
  "description": "Turns copied text into capital letters.",
  "upper.title": "Make upper case",
  "upper.keywords": ["upper", "uppercase", "capitals"],
  "empty": "There is no text to change."
}
```

```ts
import type { Actions } from "@yabbistir/api";

export const actions: Actions = {
  upper: {
    run(item, ctx) {
      const text = item?.text ?? "";
      if (text === "") return { none: true, message: yab.t("empty") };
      return { text: text.toLocaleUpperCase(ctx.language) };
    },
  },
};
```

```js
import { test } from "node:test";
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { createFakeHost } from "@yabbistir/api/fake-host";
import { actions } from "../src/index.ts";

const host = createFakeHost({ folder: new URL("..", import.meta.url) });

test("upperCases", async () => {
  assert.deepEqual(await host.run(actions.upper, { kind: "text", text: "hi" }), { text: "HI" });
});
```

- **Exports:** `actions[id].run(item, ctx)`, `detectors[id].validate(item)` / `.preview(item, ctx)`, `captureRules[id].run(item, ctx)`; each `id` matches the manifest.
- **Item:** `kind` (`text`, `code`, `link`, `color`, `image`, `file`), `text`, `url` (links; read `item.url ?? item.text`), `color`, `files`, `image`, `tags`, `copiedAt`. `item` is `null` for `"input": "none"`.
- **Context:** `ctx.language`, `ctx.preferences`, `ctx.variant`, `ctx.target` (`kind`: `finder`, `terminal`, `browser`, `editor`, `other`), `ctx.signal`.
- **Results:** `{ text }`, `{ html, text }`, `{ image }`, `{ link: { url, title? } }`, `{ file }`, `{ files }` (paths in `yab.files.workDir`), `{ none: true, message? }`. Declare it in `output`.
- **Capture rule results:** `{ keep: true }` (or nothing), `{ replace: { text } }`, `{ replace: { url } }`, `{ addToCategory: name }`, `{ ignore: true }`.
- **`accepts`:** `kinds` (required), `pattern` (an ICU regular expression *searched for* in the text or URL after trimming; write `^…$` for the whole text, `(?i)` at the start to ignore case; the syntax the store accepts is in [docs/concepts.md#patterns](docs/concepts.md#patterns)), `tags`.
- **Limits:** hint and preview 500 ms, `validate` 50 ms and synchronous, capture rule 200 ms, action 10 s, job none.
- **No effects** (no network, `exec`, notify, open, AI, translate, history) in hints, detectors, previews and capture rules.
- **Fake host:** `host.run`, `host.hint`, `host.validate`, `host.preview`, `host.capture`; `host.offers(item)` for which actions the manifest offers on an item, and `acceptsMatch(accepts, item)` for any `accepts` block; options `http`, `exec`, `ai`, `translate`, `history`, `secrets`, `preferences`, `context`, `now`; records `host.calls`, `host.progress`, `host.notifications`. Errors carry `code`: `await assert.rejects(p, { code: "permissionDenied" })`. See [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md).

## Common mistakes

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `the key "x" is not in locales/en.json` | The manifest names a key the locale file lacks | Add it; a `keywords` key's value is a list of strings |
| `"…" is not a manifest field here` (`unknownField`) | A misspelled or invented field | Check [docs/manifest.md](docs/manifest.md); the store rejects unknown fields |
| `must be a string, not null` (`schemaMismatch`) | `null` in an optional field | Leave the field out |
| `the store validator cannot verify … ` (`invalidPattern`) | `\N{…}` or a `\p{Name=Value}` in `accepts.pattern` | Use plain classes such as `[A-Za-z0-9]`, `\d`, `\p{L}` |
| A pattern that never matches | JavaScript regex syntax, or no anchors | Patterns are ICU ([the syntax](docs/concepts.md#patterns)): escape a literal `{`, use `(?i)` for case, write `^…$`; check it with `host.offers` in a test |
| `"fs" is a Node.js module` / `` `process` is a Node.js global`` | Node code in `src/`, or a library that needs Node | See [docs/errors.md#node-builtins](docs/errors.md#node-builtins) |
| `Cannot find module` / `ERR_UNSUPPORTED_TYPESCRIPT_SYNTAX` in tests | A plain `import { … } from "@yabbistir/api"`, a local import without `.ts`, an `enum`, or Node older than 22.18 | `import type`, `./file.ts`, no `enum` or `namespace`, Node 22.18+ |
| `no fake response for GET https://…` | The test did not answer that exact URL | Add it to the fake host's `http`, query string included |
| `toolMissing` in a test | The fake host's `exec` table lacks the tool | Add `exec: { tool: … }` |
| `permissionDenied` in a test | An effect in a hint or detector, a host outside `network.domains`, or a missing permission | Move the effect into `run` of an action, add the domain or the permission |
| `run returned …; expected {text}, …` (`badResult`) | `run` returned a string, or a file outside the work folder | Return a result object; write files with `yab.files.write` |
| `captureRuleTags` warning | `accepts.tags` on a capture rule | Remove it: rules see text and URLs only, never tags |
| The extension turns itself off in the app | Three failures in a row (thrown errors count in actions) | Return `{ none: true, message }` for expected cases; `validate` returns `false`, never throws |
| A `yab.ai` or `yab.translate` call fails in a hint | Hints run without effects | No `hint` on such actions; long ones are jobs |
| The action never appears in the panel | `accepts` does not match the item, or `keywords` do not start with what was typed | Check `kinds` and `pattern`; for a link, use the `link` kind |
| `npm run validate` says "not built yet (or out of date)" | There is no build, or the source changed after it, so `index.js` was not checked. It is a note, not a warning | Run `npm run build -- <id>`, then `npm run validate -- <id>`: it checks the build too, until the source changes again |
| `author` is your full name from git, not what you wanted | `npm run new` without `--author` takes `git config user.name` | Change `author` in manifest.json: your name or your GitHub user name, as you want to be credited |
| `locales/tr.json` describes "Reverse text" or another sample | It is the template's Turkish, for its sample | Translate your keys into it, or delete it: Turkish is optional |

When something is unclear, the generated references are the truth: [docs/manifest.md](docs/manifest.md) for fields, [docs/api.md](docs/api.md) for every type and `yab` function, [docs/errors.md](docs/errors.md) for every message.

File: README.md
================================================================================

# yabbistir extensions

The open extension store for [yabbistir](https://github.com/berkaygkc/yabbistir), a clipboard history app for macOS. This repository holds the extensions, the tools to write, test and build them, and the docs. An extension adds commands to the panel, recognizes what you copy, or cleans copies before they are stored. It is TypeScript bundled into one file that runs inside yabbistir, which draws everything, so every extension looks like part of the app. Each one asks for only the permissions it needs, and you decide before it is installed.

## Install extensions

In yabbistir, open Settings → Extensions → Store, pick the extensions you want, and press Install. The Store is coming in yabbistir 0.2.0. The Store reads a signed catalog only when you open it or press Refresh; yabbistir never checks in the background.

Until then, build an extension here (`npm run build -- <id>`) and install `dist/<id>-<version>.yabext` from Settings → Extensions → Development → Install .yabext….

| Extension | What it does | Permissions |
|---|---|---|
| [Download Video](extensions/dev.yabbistir.video-download) | Downloads YouTube, Instagram and X links as MP4 video or M4A audio with yt-dlp; drops the file into Finder | network, exec |
| [Link Cleaner](extensions/dev.yabbistir.link-clean) | Strips tracking parameters from links as you copy them | capture |
| [JWT](extensions/dev.yabbistir.jwt) | Recognizes copied JSON Web Tokens and shows what is inside | none |
| [Translate](extensions/dev.yabbistir.translate) | Translates and summarizes text on your Mac | none |

## Write one

You need macOS 26 or later on Apple silicon with yabbistir, and Node 24 (22.18 or later works).

1. Clone this repository and run `npm install`.
2. `npm run new -- dev.yourname.tool --template action --author <name>` creates `extensions/dev.yourname.tool/` from a template (`action`, `detector`, `capture-rule` or `job`). `--author` is how you want to be credited, your name or your GitHub user name; without it, your git user name is used and printed.
3. Edit `manifest.json`, `src/index.ts` and `locales/en.json`, and the tests in `tests/`. Only English is required: the template's `locales/tr.json` holds Turkish for its sample, so translate it or delete it.
4. `npm test -- dev.yourname.tool`, then `npm run build -- dev.yourname.tool`, then `npm run validate -- dev.yourname.tool` check it.
5. `npm run dev -- dev.yourname.tool` links it into yabbistir and rebuilds on every change. When it is ready, open a pull request.

Read next:

- [Getting started](docs/getting-started.md): a first extension, step by step.
- [Concepts](docs/concepts.md): what an extension can do, and which kind fits your idea.
- [Manifest](docs/manifest.md) and [API](docs/api.md) references, [Permissions](docs/permissions.md), [Errors](docs/errors.md).
- Guides: [jobs](docs/jobs.md), [results and targets](docs/results-and-targets.md), [detectors and previews](docs/detectors-and-previews.md), [capture rules](docs/capture-rules.md), [localization](docs/localization.md), [testing](docs/testing.md), [design guidelines](docs/design-guidelines.md).
- [Recipes](docs/concepts.md#recipes): six small, complete extensions.
- [Publishing](docs/publishing.md) and the [review checklist](docs/review-checklist.md).

Coding agents: start with [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md). [llms.txt](llms.txt) indexes the docs, and `llms-full.txt` holds them all in one file.

## Repository

```text
extensions/<id>/    the extensions, one folder each
templates/          what npm run new copies
packages/api/       the API's types (@yabbistir/api) and the fake host for tests
tools/              new, dev, validate, test, build, docs, catalog, sign, pr-checks
schema/             the manifest's and the catalog's JSON Schemas
docs/               guides and references
.github/            the pull request template, and the workflows that check, label and publish
```

## License

MIT, for the tools and the docs. Each extension states its own license in its manifest.

# Getting started

This page takes you from an empty folder to a working action: **Slugify**, which turns copied text such as `Release notes 2.0!` into `release-notes-2-0`. You will scaffold it, write it, test it without the app, and then run it in yabbistir.

You need:

- macOS 26 or later on Apple silicon, with yabbistir installed (only to try the extension in the app; writing and testing it needs nothing but Node).
- Node 24, the version the store's checks run on (Node 22.18 is the oldest that works: the tests import TypeScript directly, which older versions cannot do). `node --version` tells you; `nvm use` picks it from `.nvmrc`.
- A clone of this repository with its dependencies: `npm install` in its root folder.

Every command below runs from the repository's root folder.

## 1. Scaffold the extension

Pick an id: a reverse-domain name you control, lowercase, such as `dev.yourname.slugify`. It becomes the folder name and never changes once published.

```sh
npm run new -- dev.yourname.slugify --template action --author your-github-name
```

`--author` sets the manifest's `author`: how you want to be credited in the store, your name or your GitHub user name. Leave it out and `npm run new` uses your `git config user.name`, and prints it so you can change it in manifest.json.

This creates `extensions/dev.yourname.slugify/` from the action template:

```text
extensions/dev.yourname.slugify/
  manifest.json        what the extension is and what it adds
  src/index.ts         the code
  locales/en.json      English strings (required)
  locales/tr.json      Turkish strings (optional: translate them or delete the file)
  tests/index.test.mjs tests that run against a fake host, without the app
  README.md            what it does, an example, and why it needs each permission
  CHANGELOG.md         a "## <version>" section per version
```

The template is a working "Reverse text" action, and its files describe that sample. Replace them with the ones below:

- **Only English is required; Turkish is optional.** The template's `locales/tr.json` holds Turkish strings for its sample, so delete it, or translate your new keys into it ([Localization](localization.md)). This page deletes it.
- Its README.md and CHANGELOG.md are placeholders until you rewrite them in step 8.

## 2. The manifest

`manifest.json` tells the app everything it needs without running any code: the name, the icon, and the action, with the items it is offered on.

```json file=manifest.json
{
  "id": "dev.yourname.slugify",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "apiVersion": 1,
  "defaultLocale": "en",
  "name": "name",
  "description": "description",
  "icon": "sf:textformat.abc",
  "author": "your-github-name",
  "license": "MIT",
  "categories": ["text"],
  "contributes": {
    "actions": [
      { "id": "slugify", "title": "slugify.title", "keywords": "slugify.keywords", "input": "item",
        "accepts": { "kinds": ["text"], "pattern": "^.{1,200}$" }, "output": "text", "hint": true }
    ]
  }
}
```

What the fields mean:

- `name`, `description`, `title` and `keywords` are **keys** into `locales/en.json`, never the text itself.
- `"input": "item"` makes it a transform: it works on the item the person picked. A generator, which makes something from nothing, says `"input": "none"`.
- `accepts` decides where the action is offered, from the manifest alone; no JavaScript runs while the person types. Here it is offered on text of one line, up to 200 characters. The pattern is searched for, so `^…$` makes it match the whole text.
- `"hint": true` runs the action early and shows its result on the row, so the person sees `release-notes-2-0` before choosing it. A hint runs without effects (no network, no programs) and must finish in 500 ms. Its result is what gets pasted.
- `author` is how you want to be credited: your name or your GitHub user name. When it is the GitHub user name you commit with, a pull request by someone else that changes your extension mentions you.

Every field is in the [manifest reference](manifest.md).

## 3. The strings

```json file=locales/en.json
{
  "name": "Slugify",
  "description": "Turns copied text into a URL slug.",
  "slugify.title": "Slugify",
  "slugify.keywords": ["slug", "slugify", "url", "permalink"],
  "empty": "There is nothing to turn into a slug."
}
```

`keywords` is a list: search offers the action when one of them starts with what the person typed.

## 4. The code

`src/index.ts` exports `actions`, an object keyed by the action ids in the manifest. Each action has a `run(item, ctx)` that returns a result. The app writes the result to the clipboard, pastes it, and adds it to history; the extension never touches the clipboard itself.

```ts file=src/index.ts
import type { Actions } from "@yabbistir/api";

/** "Crème Brûlée, 2 ways!" → "creme-brulee-2-ways": ASCII letters and digits joined by single dashes. */
export function slugify(text: string): string {
  return text
    .normalize("NFKD")
    .replace(/\p{M}/gu, "") // the accents NFKD split off: é → e
    .toLowerCase()
    .replace(/ı/g, "i")
    .replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, "-")
    .replace(/^-+|-+$/g, "");
}

export const actions: Actions = {
  slugify: {
    run(item) {
      const slug = slugify(item?.text ?? "");
      // Nothing to paste: say why. The app shows the message as a calm notice.
      if (slug === "") return { none: true, message: yab.t("empty") };
      return { text: slug };
    },
  },
};
```

Three things to know about this code:

- It runs in JavaScriptCore, not Node. Web standards such as `URL`, `TextEncoder` and `fetch` are there, and so are JavaScript's own built-ins such as `Intl`. `fs`, `process`, `Buffer` and `require` are not. The global `yab` is the way to the app: here `yab.t` reads a string from the locale files in the app's language. See the [API reference](api.md).
- An expected situation, such as nothing to work on, returns `{ none: true, message }`. Throwing is for real failures: the app shows the error's message, and an action that keeps failing gets turned off.
- Helpers such as `slugify` can be exported, which makes them easy to test.

## 5. Test it

Tests run in Node against a fake host that holds the extension to the app's rules: it reads the manifest's permissions, refuses what the app would refuse, and never touches the network or runs a program. `host.run` runs an action the way a person's choice does, and `host.hint` runs it as a hint, without effects.

```js file=tests/index.test.mjs
import { describe, test } from "node:test";
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { createFakeHost } from "@yabbistir/api/fake-host";

import { actions, slugify } from "../src/index.ts";

const host = createFakeHost({ folder: new URL("..", import.meta.url) });
const text = (value) => ({ kind: "text", text: value });

describe("slugify", () => {
  test("makesASlug", async () => {
    assert.deepEqual(await host.run(actions.slugify, text("Release notes 2.0!")), { text: "release-notes-2-0" });
  });

  test("dropsAccents", () => {
    assert.equal(slugify("Crème Brûlée, 2 ways!"), "creme-brulee-2-ways");
  });

  test("worksAsAHint", async () => {
    // A hint runs before the person picks the row, without effects; its result is the one pasted.
    assert.deepEqual(await host.hint(actions.slugify, text("Hello, World")), { text: "hello-world" });
  });

  test("saysSoWhenNothingIsLeft", async () => {
    assert.deepEqual(await host.run(actions.slugify, text("!!!")), { none: true, message: "There is nothing to turn into a slug." });
  });
});
```

The fake host fills in what an item needs (`id`, `tags`, `copiedAt`), so a test passes only what matters. Run the tests and the checks:

```sh
npm test -- dev.yourname.slugify
npm run validate -- dev.yourname.slugify
```

`npm run validate` prints one line per problem: the file, the field, what was wrong and how to fix it. There is no build yet, so it also notes "not built yet (or out of date)": the build in the next step makes `index.js` and checks it. [Testing](testing.md) covers the fake host in full, and [Errors](errors.md) lists every message.

## 6. Build it

```sh
npm run build -- dev.yourname.slugify
```

The build bundles `src/index.ts` and everything it imports into one `dist/dev.yourname.slugify/index.js`, copies the manifest, the locales, the README and the CHANGELOG next to it, checks that folder with the store's rules, and packs it into `dist/dev.yourname.slugify-1.0.0.yabext`. If the code imports a Node module or uses a Node global, the build stops and says so ([why](errors.md#node-builtins)). From now on, `npm run validate` checks this build too, `index.js` included, as long as it is newer than your source; after a change it notes "not built yet (or out of date)" until you build again.

## 7. Run it in yabbistir

```sh
npm run dev -- dev.yourname.slugify
```

`npm run dev` builds the extension and links `dist/dev.yourname.slugify` into `~/Library/Application Support/yabbistir/Extensions/`. The app lists it in Settings → Extensions with the source "Development" and reloads it whenever the files change. `npm run dev` keeps watching `src/`, `locales/` and the manifest and rebuilds on every save; stop it with Ctrl-C. It never replaces a real folder: if an installed copy with the same id is there, remove that copy in Settings first.

Then, in yabbistir: copy a sentence, press ⇧⌘V, and type `slug`. The row shows the hint; ↵ pastes the slug. Or select a text item and press ⇧ to see every transform for it.

`console.log` in your code writes to Settings → Extensions → Development → Log, together with the extension's errors.

## 8. Finish

Before you call it done:

- Rewrite `README.md`: what the extension does, an example, and why it needs each permission (Slugify needs none).
- Keep `CHANGELOG.md` with a `## 1.0.0` section.
- `npm test`, `npm run validate` and `npm run build` pass for your id.

To share it, open a pull request: see [Publishing](publishing.md).

## Where next

- [Concepts](concepts.md): items, actions, detectors, capture rules, jobs, and which one fits your idea.
- [Recipes](concepts.md#recipes): six small, complete extensions to start from.
- [Design guidelines](design-guidelines.md): names, icons and words that fit the app.


================================================================================
File: docs/concepts.md
================================================================================

# Concepts

An extension is a folder: a `manifest.json` that says what it adds, a `src/index.ts` that does the work, and strings in `locales/`. The app reads the manifest to decide where the extension appears, and calls into its code only when there is work to do. The extension computes and returns plain data. The app draws every row, chip, preview, card and notice, in its own calm grey look, so an extension never picks a color or lays anything out.

## Where the code runs

yabbistir runs extensions in a helper process, each in its own JavaScriptCore context, isolated from the app and from each other. The language level is ES2022.

- **There:** JavaScript's built-ins (`JSON`, `Math`, `Intl`, `RegExp`, `Map`, `Promise` …), the web standards listed under [Globals](api.md#globals) (`URL`, `URLSearchParams`, `TextEncoder`, `TextDecoder`, `atob`, `btoa`, `setTimeout`, `AbortController`, `crypto.getRandomValues`, `crypto.randomUUID`, `fetch`, `console`), and the global `yab`, the extension's way to the app ([The yab object](api.md#the-yab-object)).
- **Not there:** anything from Node (`fs`, `path`, `child_process`, `process`, `Buffer`, `require`) or from a browser page (`document`, `window`, `localStorage`). The build refuses Node modules and globals; see [errors](errors.md#node-builtins) for what to use instead.
- **npm packages** that are plain JavaScript are bundled into the one `index.js` by the build. A package that needs Node will not work.
- `console.log` writes to Settings → Extensions → Development → Log.

## The item

An action, detector or rule gets the clipboard **item** it is about ([`Item`](api.md#item)):

| `kind` | What it carries |
|---|---|
| `text`, `code` | `text` |
| `link` | `url` (and often `text`); read it as `item.url ?? item.text` |
| `color` | `color`: `hex`, `r`, `g`, `b` (0–255), `a` (0–1) |
| `image` | `image`: a handle to pass to `yab.image`, `yab.vision` or return; the pixels stay in the app |
| `file` | `files`: `path`, `name`, `size`, `uti` for each |

Every item also has `id`, `tags` (set by detectors, as `"extension.id:detector"`), `copiedAt` (ISO 8601), and sometimes `source` (the app it was copied from) and `richText.html`. Copies that apps mark as concealed, such as passwords, never reach an extension.

## The context

Each call also gets a **context** ([`Context`](api.md#context)): `language` (the app's language, such as `"en"` or `"tr"`), `preferences` (the extension's settings), `variant` (the chosen variant's id), `target` (the app the result is headed for: `bundleID`, `name` and a `kind` of `finder`, `terminal`, `browser`, `editor` or `other`), `trigger` (where the call came from) and `signal` (aborts when the person cancels).

## Actions

An **action** is a command in the panel. Its manifest entry says what it is called, which items it takes and what it returns; `actions[id].run(item, ctx)` in `src/index.ts` does the work and returns a [result](results-and-targets.md).

- **Transforms** (`"input": "item"`) work on an item: Base64-encode it, download the video a link points to. `accepts` says which items: `kinds`, an optional regular expression `pattern` over the text or URL, and optional detector `tags`.
- **Generators** (`"input": "none"`) make something from nothing, such as a UUID. `run` gets `null` for the item.
- **Variants** are ready-made choices of one action, each its own row: "Download as video" and "Download audio". `ctx.variant` says which one was chosen.
- **Hints** (`"hint": true`) run the action before it is picked, without effects, and show the result on the row. The result shown is the one pasted. A hint that returns `{ none: true }` leaves the action offered, and its row shows no preview.
- **Jobs** (`"job": true`) are long actions: a card under the menu bar icon shows their progress and lets the person cancel. See [Jobs](jobs.md).

Where actions appear:

- **Search:** typing in the panel (⇧⌘V) offers an action when one of its keywords starts with what was typed (two letters or more). A transform also needs the selected item to match `accepts`; a generator always qualifies.
- **The ⇧ panel:** ⇧ on an item lists every transform that accepts it.
- **⌘K:** the full action list for an item.

Actions whose `targets` include the paste target's kind come first, and `targetsOnly` keeps an action to those targets alone. ↵ pastes the result into the app the panel opened for; ⌘C copies it instead.

**Which actions appear is decided from manifests alone.** No extension code runs on a keystroke. A hint runs once its row is shown.

## Patterns

`accepts.pattern` (on actions, detectors and capture rules) is a regular expression in **ICU** syntax, the kind macOS uses, not JavaScript's. It is *searched for* in the item's text, or its URL for a link, after surrounding whitespace is trimmed: write `^…$` to match the whole text. Matching is case-sensitive unless the pattern starts with `(?i)`.

The store accepts only what it can check against the app, so `npm run validate` refuses anything else with [`invalidPattern`](errors.md#invalidpattern). What it accepts:

- **Plain syntax:** literals, `.`, `^`, `$`, `|`, groups `( )`, `(?: )`, named groups `(?<name> )` with `\k<name>`, back references `\1`.
- **Quantifiers:** `*`, `+`, `?`, `{n}`, `{n,}`, `{n,m}`, lazy (`*?`) and possessive (`*+`) forms, atomic groups `(?> )`.
- **Look-around:** `(?= )`, `(?! )`, and look-behind `(?<= )`, `(?<! )` of bounded length (no `*`, `+` or `{n,}` inside).
- **Flags:** `(?i)` (ignore case), `(?m)`, `(?s)`, `(?x)`, `(?w)`, at the start or scoped as `(?i: )`.
- **Escapes:** `\d`, `\w`, `\s` and their capitals (`\d` is any decimal digit, not only 0–9), `\b`, `\B`, `\A`, `\z`, `\Z`, `\t`, `\n`, `\r`, `\xhh`, `\x{h…}`, `\uhhhh`, `\Q…\E`, `\X`. Escape a literal `{` as `\{`.
- **Sets:** `[abc]`, `[^a-z]`, nested sets `[[a-z][0-9]]`, intersection `[\p{L}&&[a-z]]`, difference `[a-z--[aeiou]]`, and POSIX classes in lowercase (`[[:alpha:]]`, `[[:digit:]]`).
- **Unicode properties**, with `\p{…}`, or `\P{…}` for the opposite, spelled exactly as ICU spells them:
  - general categories: `\p{L}`, `\p{Lu}`, `\p{Ll}`, `\p{N}`, `\p{Nd}`, `\p{P}`, `\p{S}`, `\p{Z}`, or long names such as `\p{Letter}` and `\p{Uppercase_Letter}`;
  - scripts: `\p{Latin}`, `\p{Greek}`, `\p{Cyrillic}`, `\p{Arabic}`, `\p{Han}`, `\p{Hiragana}`, …;
  - binary properties: `\p{Alphabetic}`, `\p{White_Space}`, `\p{Emoji}`, `\p{ASCII}`, `\p{Any}`, …;
  - blocks with `In`: `\p{InBasic_Latin}`;
  - and the `=` forms of those four only: `\p{gc=Lu}`, `\p{Script=Latin}`, `\p{scx=Latin}`, `\p{Block=Basic_Latin}`.

  [`tools/lib/icu-properties.json`](../tools/lib/icu-properties.json) lists every spelling the store accepts.

Refused, because the store cannot verify them: character names (`\N{…}`), any other `\p{Name=Value}` (`Name=`, `Age=`, `Line_Break=`, `East_Asian_Width=`, `Numeric_Value=`, `Bidi_Class=` …), spellings off the list (`\p{IsL}`, `\p{L&}`, `\p{all}`, `[[:ALPHA:]]`, extra spaces), and an unbounded look-behind. Refused because ICU rejects them: JavaScript-only syntax such as a bare `{`, `[^]` or an empty pattern.

In tests, [`host.offers(item)` and `acceptsMatch(accepts, item)`](testing.md#where-an-action-is-offered) apply a manifest's `accepts` to a sample item, close to the app's matching.

## Detectors

A **detector** tags items as they are copied: a JWT, an issue key, a timestamp. Its manifest entry names the tag and `accepts` the items it looks at; an optional `validate(item)` has the last word, quickly and without promises. A detector can also add sections (text, code, key-value rows, an image, a link) to a tagged item's preview, and actions can be offered only on items with a tag. A new detector scans the existing history once, in the background. See [Detectors and previews](detectors-and-previews.md).

## Capture rules

A **capture rule** sees each new copy before it is stored and decides: keep it, store a cleaned version instead, put it in a category too, or do not store it at all. Rules need the `capture` permission, see text and URLs only (never tags or pixels), and have 200 ms. See [Capture rules](capture-rules.md).

## Calls with effects and calls without

Some calls happen because the person chose something: running an action or a job. Those may use the network, run programs, show notices, open links, ask the on-device model or translate, as far as the extension's permissions allow.

Other calls happen on their own: hints, detector checks, previews and capture rules. They run without effects: `yab.http.fetch`, `fetch`, `yab.exec`, `yab.notify`, `yab.open`, `yab.ai`, `yab.translate` and `yab.history` reject or throw `permissionDenied` there. They can still read the item, the preferences, secrets and storage, and use pure functions such as `yab.t`.

## Time limits

| Call | Limit |
|---|---|
| Hint, and a detector's preview | 500 ms |
| Detector `validate` | 50 ms, no promises |
| Capture rule | 200 ms (then it is skipped and the copy is stored as it is) |
| Action | 10 seconds |
| Job | none; the person can cancel it |

A call that runs over is cut off.

## When something goes wrong

- A `run` that throws fails: the app shows "Extension failed" with the extension's name and the error's message. Write messages for people, with `yab.t`.
- Three failures in a row turn the extension off; Settings shows it as off and the person is told. Failures that are not the extension's fault do not count: `cancelled`, `interrupted`, `toolMissing`, `networkError` and `permissionDenied`. A job's thrown error does not count either; only a broken result (`badResult`, `notFound`, `syntax`) does.
- So an expected situation (nothing to do, input of the wrong shape) returns `{ none: true, message }` rather than throwing, and a detector's `validate` returns `false` rather than throwing.

Every error code is in [errors](errors.md#runtime-errors).

## Permissions

An extension starts with no permissions, and most need none: text transforms, detectors, on-device AI and translation, image work and files in the call's work folder are all free. Four permissions exist, each shown to the person before install: `network`, `exec`, `capture` and `history`. See [Permissions](permissions.md).

## Which contribution point fits an idea

| Idea | Use | Start from |
|---|---|---|
| Change a copy when the person asks (encode, reformat, convert), and paste the result | An action, `"input": "item"`; no permission | `--template action`, [Getting started](getting-started.md) |
| Change every copy automatically, as it is copied (clean, rewrite, drop) | A capture rule; needs `capture`, which the person reads as "Can see everything you copy" | `--template capture-rule`, [A link-cleaning rule](recipes/link-cleaning-rule.md) |
| Mark copies for the person, without changing them | A detector: its tag shows as a chip on the item; no permission | `--template detector`, [Tag and preview](recipes/tag-and-preview.md) |
| Make something new (UUID, timestamp, lorem ipsum) | An action, `"input": "none"` | `--template action` |
| A few fixed flavors of one action (to Turkish / to English) | `variants` on one action | [Translate and summarize](recipes/translate-and-summarize.md) |
| Show the result before it is chosen | `"hint": true` | [Getting started](getting-started.md) |
| Something that takes seconds or minutes (download, convert) | An action with `"job": true` | `--template job`, [Download with yt-dlp](recipes/download-with-yt-dlp.md) |
| Hand a file to Finder | An action with `"output": "file"` and `"targets": ["finder"]` | [Drop a file into Finder](recipes/drop-a-file-in-finder.md) |
| Recognize a kind of text (token, key, ID) and explain it | A detector with `validate` and `preview` | `--template detector`, [Tag and preview](recipes/tag-and-preview.md) |
| Offer an action only on items a detector tagged | `accepts.tags` on the action | [Tag and preview](recipes/tag-and-preview.md) |
| Call a web service | An action with the `network` permission | [Call an API with a key](recipes/call-an-api-with-a-key.md) |
| Run a command-line program | An action or job with the `exec` permission | `--template job` |
| Summarize, rewrite or translate on the Mac | `yab.ai.generate`, `yab.translate` (no permission) | [Translate and summarize](recipes/translate-and-summarize.md) |
| Work with earlier copies | `yab.history` (the `history` permission) | [Permissions](permissions.md#history) |

**A capture rule cannot show a tag or a chip.** Only detectors tag items, and they run after the copy is stored, so a rule never sees tags or adds them. To change copies and mark them too, put a rule and a detector in one extension.

Not possible: drawing your own interface, running in the background on a timer, reading the clipboard directly, writing outside the call's work folder, reaching the network from a detector or a rule.

## Several contributions in one extension

One extension can add any mix of actions, detectors and capture rules. Scaffold with the template nearest to the main thing it does, then add the others by hand:

1. In `manifest.json`, add the other lists under `contributes` (`actions`, `detectors`, `captureRules`), each entry with its own id. Copy an entry's shape from the [manifest reference](manifest.md) or from the template that has it.
2. In `src/index.ts`, export the matching objects, keyed by those ids: `export const detectors: Detectors = { … }` next to `export const actions: Actions = { … }`.
3. Add every new string key to `locales/en.json`, and tests for each part.

Permissions belong to the whole extension: a capture rule needs `capture` even when the rest of the extension needs nothing, and the person sees it for the whole extension. [Tag and preview](recipes/tag-and-preview.md) is a detector and an action in one extension, the action offered only on the detector's tag.

## Recipes

Each recipe is a small, complete extension: manifest, strings, code and tests that pass `npm run validate`, `npm run build` and `npm test`.

- [Download video and audio with yt-dlp](recipes/download-with-yt-dlp.md): a job that runs a program and returns a file.
- [Call an API with a key](recipes/call-an-api-with-a-key.md): the `network` permission and a secret preference.
- [Tag and preview](recipes/tag-and-preview.md): a detector with `validate` and `preview`, and an action offered on its tag.
- [A link-cleaning rule](recipes/link-cleaning-rule.md): a capture rule that rewrites links.
- [Translate and summarize on the Mac](recipes/translate-and-summarize.md): `yab.translate` and `yab.ai`.
- [Drop a file into Finder](recipes/drop-a-file-in-finder.md): a file result aimed at Finder.

<!-- Generated by `npm run docs` from schema/manifest.schema.json. Do not edit this file: change the source and run npm run docs. -->

# Manifest reference

`manifest.json` sits at the root of an extension's folder, next to `src/` and `locales/`. This page lists every field [the schema](../schema/manifest.schema.json) allows.

Every text a person reads (names, titles, keywords, tags) is a key into `locales/<language>.json`, never the text itself; see [Localization](localization.md). Run `npm run validate -- <id>` after each change: it names the field, what was expected and how to fix it ([every message](errors.md)).

Sections: [Top level](#top-level) · [`network`](#network) · [`requires`](#requires) · [`requires.tools[]`](#requirestools) · [`preferences[]`](#preferences) · [`preferences[].options[]`](#preferencesoptions) · [`contributes`](#contributes) · [`contributes.actions[]`](#contributesactions) · [`accepts`](#accepts) · [`contributes.actions[].variants[]`](#contributesactionsvariants) · [`contributes.detectors[]`](#contributesdetectors) · [`contributes.captureRules[]`](#contributescapturerules) · [Rules beyond the schema](#rules-beyond-the-schema) · [A complete example](#a-complete-example)

## Top level

| Field | Type | Required | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string matching `^[a-z0-9]+(\.[a-z0-9-]+)+$` | yes | Reverse-domain id; equals the folder name. Use a name you control, such as `dev.yourname.tool`, and never change it once published: the app recognizes updates by it. |
| `version` | string matching `^\d+\.\d+\.\d+(-[0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?$` | yes | Raise it in every pull request that changes the extension, and add a matching `## <version>` section to CHANGELOG.md. |
| `apiVersion` | `1` | yes | Always `1`. |
| `minAppVersion` | string |  | The oldest yabbistir version the extension works with, such as `"0.2.0"`. Leave it out unless you rely on something a newer app added; an older app lists the extension but does not install it. |
| `defaultLocale` | string | yes | A language with a locales/<language>.json file, usually "en". Strings missing in the app's language come from this locale. The store also requires `locales/en.json`. |
| `name` | [locale key](localization.md) | yes | The extension's name in Settings, in the Store and on its notices. |
| `description` | [locale key](localization.md) | yes | One sentence for the Store and Settings. |
| `icon` | string | yes | "sf:<SF Symbol name>" or a file name in the extension folder. A file icon must be `icon.png` next to manifest.json: the build copies only that name. See [Design guidelines](design-guidelines.md#icons). |
| `author` | string | yes | How you want to be credited: your name or your GitHub user name. When someone else's pull request changes the extension, a comment names the author, and mentions them if it is the GitHub user name they committed the extension with. `npm run new` takes it from `--author <name>`, or else from `git config user.name` and then prints the name it used. |
| `license` | string | yes | An SPDX license id. The store accepts `MIT`, `Apache-2.0`, `BSD-2-Clause`, `BSD-3-Clause`, `ISC`, `MPL-2.0`; MIT is the usual choice. |
| `categories` | list of one of `"text"`, `"links"`, `"images"`, `"files"`, `"developer"`, `"media"`, `"ai"`, `"productivity"` |  | Where the Store files the extension. Pick one or two. |
| `permissions` | list of one of `"network"`, `"exec"`, `"capture"`, `"history"` |  | "capture" is required by captureRules. Leave it out when the extension needs none. Each one is shown to the person before install; see [Permissions](permissions.md). |
| `network` | object, see [`network`](#network) |  | With the `network` permission: the hosts the extension may reach. An empty list, or no `network` at all, means any host, and the person is told so. |
| `requires` | object, see [`requires`](#requires) |  | With the `exec` permission: the programs the extension runs with `yab.exec`. |
| `preferences` | list of objects, see [`preferences[]`](#preferences) |  | Settings the app draws for the extension. Their values reach `yab.preferences` and `ctx.preferences`, except secrets, which only `yab.secrets.get` reads. |
| `contributes` | object, see [`contributes`](#contributes) |  | What the extension adds. Each id here is a key of the matching export of `src/index.ts`: `actions`, `detectors` or `captureRules`. |

No other fields: the store rejects any it does not know ([`unknownField`](errors.md#unknownfield)).

## `network`

| Field | Type | Required | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `domains` | list of string matching `^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?(\.[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?)*$` | yes | Lowercase host names: no scheme, no path, no *. A host matches a domain when it is the domain or ends with `.` and the domain, so `youtube.com` covers `www.youtube.com`. Redirects must stay inside the list. |

No other fields: the store rejects any it does not know ([`unknownField`](errors.md#unknownfield)).

## `requires`

| Field | Type | Required | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tools` | list of objects, see [`requires.tools[]`](#requirestools) | yes | Required with the "exec" permission, and only allowed with it. |

No other fields: the store rejects any it does not know ([`unknownField`](errors.md#unknownfield)).

## `requires.tools[]`

| Field | Type | Required | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string matching `^[A-Za-z0-9._+-]+$` | yes | The command's name. It is looked for in `/opt/homebrew/bin`, then `/usr/local/bin`, then the system's folders. |
| `install` | non-empty string | yes | Shown in Settings when the tool is missing, as a command to copy, such as `brew install yt-dlp`. |

No other fields: the store rejects any it does not know ([`unknownField`](errors.md#unknownfield)).

## `preferences[]`

| Field | Type | Required | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string matching `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$` | yes | The key in `yab.preferences`, or the id for `yab.secrets.get`. |
| `type` | one of `"text"`, `"toggle"`, `"choice"`, `"secret"`, `"folder"` | yes | `text`: a line of text. `toggle`: `true` or `false`. `choice`: one of `options`; the value is the option's id. `secret`: kept in the Keychain, read only with `yab.secrets.get`. `folder`: a folder the person picks; the value is an absolute path. |
| `title` | [locale key](localization.md) | yes | The label in Settings. |
| `default` | any |  | Not allowed for "secret"; for "folder" a path starting with ~, such as ~/Downloads. The value until the person changes it: text, `true`/`false` or an option id. |
| `confirm` | [locale key](localization.md) |  | Question asked before the preference is turned on. |
| `options` | list of objects, see [`preferences[].options[]`](#preferencesoptions) |  | The choices of a `choice` preference. |

No other fields: the store rejects any it does not know ([`unknownField`](errors.md#unknownfield)).

## `preferences[].options[]`

| Field | Type | Required | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string matching `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$` | yes | The preference's value when this option is chosen. |
| `title` | [locale key](localization.md) | yes | The option's label in Settings. |

## `contributes`

| Field | Type | Required | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actions` | list of objects, see [`contributes.actions[]`](#contributesactions) |  | Transforms and generators; see [Concepts](concepts.md#actions). |
| `detectors` | list of objects, see [`contributes.detectors[]`](#contributesdetectors) |  | See [Detectors and previews](detectors-and-previews.md). |
| `captureRules` | list of objects, see [`contributes.captureRules[]`](#contributescapturerules) |  | Needs the "capture" permission. See [Capture rules](capture-rules.md). |

No other fields: the store rejects any it does not know ([`unknownField`](errors.md#unknownfield)).

## `contributes.actions[]`

| Field | Type | Required | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string matching `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$` | yes | The key of `actions` in `src/index.ts`. |
| `title` | [locale key](localization.md) | yes | The row's title in the panel. |
| `subtitle` | [locale key](localization.md) |  | The row's second line when it has no hint; a variant's own subtitle wins. |
| `keywords` | [locale key](localization.md) | yes | Its locale value is an array of keywords. Search offers the action when one of its keywords starts with what the person typed (two letters or more). |
| `input` | one of `"item"`, `"none"` | yes | `item`: a transform; it gets the selected item. `none`: a generator; it makes something from nothing (a UUID) and gets `null`. |
| `accepts` | object, see [`accepts`](#accepts) | when `input` is `"item"` | The items the action is offered on. |
| `output` | one of `"text"`, `"html"`, `"image"`, `"link"`, `"file"`, `"files"`, `"none"` | yes | What `run` returns: `text` `{ text }`, `html` `{ html, text }`, `image` `{ image }`, `link` `{ link }`, `file` `{ file }`, `files` `{ files }`, `none` `{ none: true }`. See [Results and targets](results-and-targets.md). |
| `targets` | list of one of `"finder"`, `"terminal"`, `"browser"`, `"editor"`, `"other"` |  | Paste targets where the action leads the list. |
| `targetsOnly` | boolean |  | Only offered when the paste target is one of "targets"; needs a non-empty "targets". |
| `job` | boolean |  | Runs as a long-running job. See [Jobs](jobs.md). Without it, `run` must finish in 10 seconds. |
| `verb` | [locale key](localization.md) |  | A job's label in the ⇧ panel: "↵ <verb> · ⌘C <verb> and copy", such as "Download". Without it a job says "Start". |
| `failTitle` | [locale key](localization.md) |  | A failed job's title, such as "Couldn't download the video"; a variant's own wins. |
| `variants` | list of objects, see [`contributes.actions[].variants[]`](#contributesactionsvariants) |  | Ready-made choices of one action. Each is its own row, and `ctx.variant` is the chosen id. |
| `hint` | boolean |  | Run early (500 ms limit) and show the output as the row's hint. The hint run has no effects (no network, programs, notices, AI or translation), and its result is what is pasted when the person picks the row, so it must be the real answer. A hint that returns `{ none: true }` leaves the action offered, with no preview on its row. Never for jobs or `file`/`files` output. |
| `priority` | integer |  | Orders the extension's own actions on an item, highest first. Defaults to 0. |

No other fields: the store rejects any it does not know ([`unknownField`](errors.md#unknownfield)).

## `accepts`

Used by actions, detectors and capture rules.

| Field | Type | Required | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kinds` | list (at least 1) of one of `"text"`, `"code"`, `"link"`, `"color"`, `"image"`, `"file"` | yes | `image` also takes a file item that is an image. |
| `pattern` | string |  | ICU regular expression matched against the item's text or URL. Searched for, not matched whole: write `^…$` to match the whole text. Surrounding whitespace is trimmed first. [Patterns](concepts.md#patterns) lists the ICU syntax the store accepts. |
| `tags` | list of string |  | "tag" (own detector) or "extension.id:tag". Only items that carry one of these tags. |

No other fields: the store rejects any it does not know ([`unknownField`](errors.md#unknownfield)).

## `contributes.actions[].variants[]`

| Field | Type | Required | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string matching `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$` | yes | What `ctx.variant` holds when this variant is chosen. |
| `title` | [locale key](localization.md) | yes | The variant's row title. |
| `subtitle` | [locale key](localization.md) |  | The variant's second line. |
| `failTitle` | [locale key](localization.md) |  | The job card's title when this variant fails. |

No other fields: the store rejects any it does not know ([`unknownField`](errors.md#unknownfield)).

## `contributes.detectors[]`

| Field | Type | Required | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string matching `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$` | yes | The key of `detectors` in `src/index.ts`. A tagged item carries `<extension id>:<detector id>` in `item.tags`. |
| `tag` | [locale key](localization.md) | yes | The chip shown on a tagged item: one short word. |
| `accepts` | object, see [`accepts`](#accepts) | yes | The items the detector looks at. |
| `validate` | boolean |  | `true`: once `accepts` matches, `detectors[id].validate(item)` decides. It must answer at once, without a promise. |
| `preview` | boolean |  | `true`: `detectors[id].preview(item, ctx)` adds sections to a tagged item's preview. |
| `suggests` | list of string |  | Action ids to bring forward on a tagged item. Accepted, but this version of the app does not use it yet. |

No other fields: the store rejects any it does not know ([`unknownField`](errors.md#unknownfield)).

## `contributes.captureRules[]`

| Field | Type | Required | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string matching `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$` | yes | The key of `captureRules` in `src/index.ts`. |
| `title` | [locale key](localization.md) | yes | Shown in Settings, where the person can turn each rule off. |
| `description` | [locale key](localization.md) |  | One sentence under the title in Settings. |
| `accepts` | object, see [`accepts`](#accepts) | yes | The copies the rule runs on. Never use `tags` here: rules run before any tag exists. |

No other fields: the store rejects any it does not know ([`unknownField`](errors.md#unknownfield)).

## Rules beyond the schema

`npm run validate` also checks what a schema cannot say:

- `id` equals the extension's folder name.
- `locales/<defaultLocale>.json` exists and holds every key the manifest uses; `locales/en.json` exists and holds them all too.
- A `keywords` key's value is a list of strings in the locale file: `"reverse.keywords": ["reverse", "flip"]`.
- `captureRules` need the `capture` permission; `exec` needs `requires.tools`, and `requires.tools` needs `exec`.
- Ids are unique within their list (actions, variants of one action, detectors, capture rules, preferences).
- A `secret` preference has no `default`; a `folder` default starts with `~`; a `choice` has `options`.
- `targetsOnly` needs at least one entry in `targets`.
- `accepts.pattern` compiles as an ICU regular expression, the kind the app uses.
- README.md and CHANGELOG.md exist, and, once built, so does `index.js`.

## A complete example

The manifest of [Download Video](../extensions/dev.yabbistir.video-download), which uses most fields:

```json
{
  "id": "dev.yabbistir.video-download",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "apiVersion": 1,
  "defaultLocale": "en",
  "name": "name",
  "description": "description",
  "icon": "sf:arrow.down.circle",
  "author": "Berkay Gökçe",
  "license": "MIT",
  "categories": ["files"],
  "permissions": ["network", "exec"],
  "network": { "domains": ["youtube.com", "youtu.be", "instagram.com", "x.com", "twitter.com"] },
  "requires": {
    "tools": [
      { "name": "yt-dlp", "install": "brew install yt-dlp" },
      { "name": "ffmpeg", "install": "brew install ffmpeg" },
      { "name": "deno", "install": "brew install deno" }
    ]
  },
  "preferences": [
    { "id": "browserCookies", "type": "choice", "title": "cookies.title", "default": "off", "confirm": "cookies.confirm",
      "options": [
        { "id": "off", "title": "cookies.off" },
        { "id": "safari", "title": "cookies.safari" },
        { "id": "chrome", "title": "cookies.chrome" },
        { "id": "firefox", "title": "cookies.firefox" }
      ] }
  ],
  "contributes": {
    "actions": [
      { "id": "download", "title": "download.title", "keywords": "download.keywords", "input": "item",
        "accepts": { "kinds": ["link"], "pattern": "^https?://([a-z0-9-]+\\.)*(youtube\\.com|youtu\\.be|instagram\\.com|x\\.com|twitter\\.com)/" },
        "targets": ["finder"], "job": true, "output": "file", "verb": "verb",
        "variants": [
          { "id": "video", "title": "video.title", "subtitle": "video.subtitle", "failTitle": "video.fail" },
          { "id": "audio", "title": "audio.title", "subtitle": "audio.subtitle", "failTitle": "audio.fail" }
        ] }
    ]
  }
}
```

<!-- Generated by `npm run docs` from packages/api/index.d.ts. Do not edit this file: change the source and run npm run docs. -->

# API reference

@yabbistir/api — the extension API, version 1.

An extension's index.ts exports `actions`, `detectors` and/or `captureRules`. yabbistir draws every piece of UI;
an extension only computes. The functions below run in JavaScriptCore (ES2022), not Node: there
is no `require`, `process`, `fs` or `Buffer`. The web standards declared at the bottom are there.

In TypeScript, `import type { Actions, Item } from "@yabbistir/api";` brings these types in, and the globals come with them. The blocks below are the declarations as they are in `packages/api/index.d.ts`.

Contents: [What an extension exports](#what-an-extension-exports) · [What a call gets](#what-a-call-gets) · [What a call returns](#what-a-call-returns) · [The yab object](#the-yab-object) · [Types used by yab](#types-used-by-yab) · [Errors](#errors) · [Globals](#globals)

## What an extension exports

`src/index.ts` exports any of `actions`, `detectors` and `captureRules`, each an object keyed by the ids in manifest.json.

### Actions

```ts snippet
export type Actions = Record<string, Action>;
```

### Action

```ts snippet
export interface Action {
  /** `item` is null for actions whose manifest says `"input": "none"`. */
  run(item: Item | null, ctx: Context): Result | Promise<Result>;
}
```

### Detectors

```ts snippet
export type Detectors = Record<string, Detector>;
```

### Detector

```ts snippet
export interface Detector {
  /** Keep the tag? Runs in at most 50 ms; no promises. */
  validate?(item: Item): boolean;
  /** Blocks for the preview of an item carrying this detector's tag. */
  preview?(item: Item, ctx: Context): PreviewSection[] | Promise<PreviewSection[]>;
}
```

### CaptureRules

```ts snippet
export type CaptureRules = Record<string, CaptureRule>;
```

### CaptureRule

Runs on each new copy before it reaches history, in at most 200 ms (or it is skipped); needs the
"capture" permission. Rules run one at a time, each seeing what the ones before it made of the copy.
Rules run in the order extensions are listed in Settings, then in manifest order. A copy whose text or
link is over 256 KB meets no rule and is stored as it is. No network, programs, history, AI,
translation, notifications or opening links; `ctx.trigger` is "capture".

Capture rules see text and URLs only: no tags, no pixels.

```ts snippet
export interface CaptureRule {
  run(item: Item, ctx: Context): CaptureResult | undefined | Promise<CaptureResult | undefined>;
}
```

### CaptureResult

What a capture rule decides about a new copy.
- `keep`: store it as it is. Returning nothing (`undefined` or `null`) does the same.
- `ignore`: do not store it; the rules after this one do not run.
- `replace`: store this plain text or link instead (a non-empty string). Only for text, code and link
  copies; on any other copy it is ignored. The next rule sees the replaced copy.
- `addToCategory`: also put it in this category, which must exist (case and accents are ignored); an
  unknown name is ignored.

Anything else is an error, and the rule is skipped for this copy.

```ts snippet
export type CaptureResult =
  | { keep: true }
  | { ignore: true }
  | { replace: { text: string } }
  | { replace: { url: string } }
  | { addToCategory: string };
```

## What a call gets

### Item

A clipboard item. Concealed copies (passwords) never reach an extension.

```ts snippet
export interface Item {
  id: number;
  kind: "text" | "code" | "link" | "color" | "image" | "file";
  /** Text and code items. */
  text?: string;
  /** Link items. */
  url?: string;
  /** Color items: 0–255 channels, alpha 0–1. */
  color?: { hex: string; r: number; g: number; b: number; a: number };
  /** File items. */
  files?: { path: string; name: string; size: number; uti: string }[];
  /** Items copied as rich text. */
  richText?: { html?: string };
  /** Image items. */
  image?: ImageHandle;
  /** Tags detectors put on the item, as "extension.id:tag". */
  tags: string[];
  /** Where it was copied. */
  source?: { name?: string | null; bundleID?: string | null; device: string };
  /** ISO 8601. */
  copiedAt: string;
}
```

### Context

What a call knows besides the item.

```ts snippet
export interface Context {
  /** The app's language, e.g. "en" or "tr". */
  language: string;
  /** This extension's preferences (manifest defaults until the user changes them). */
  preferences: Record<string, unknown>;
  /** Where the call came from. */
  trigger: "search" | "shiftPanel" | "commandK" | "detect" | "preview" | "capture";
  /** The variant the user chose, for actions with `variants`. */
  variant: string | null;
  /** The app the result is headed for, when known. */
  target: { bundleID: string; name: string; kind: "finder" | "terminal" | "browser" | "editor" | "other" } | null;
  /**
   * Aborts when the person cancels the call (a job's ✕). Its `reason` is a YabError with code
   * "cancelled", and pending `yab` promises reject with that code too. Stop work and let the error
   * through; whatever the call returns afterwards is dropped.
   */
  signal: AbortSignal;
}
```

### ImageHandle

A handle to an image held by yabbistir; pass it to `yab.image`, `yab.vision` or return it.

```ts snippet
export interface ImageHandle {
  readonly __image: string;
  readonly width: number;
  readonly height: number;
}
```

## What a call returns

### Result

What an action returns. yabbistir writes it to the clipboard, pastes it and adds it to history.

```ts snippet
export type Result =
  | { text: string }
  | { html: string; text: string }
  | { image: ImageHandle }
  | { link: { url: string; title?: string } }
  | { file: string }
  | { files: string[] }
  | { none: true; message?: string };
```

### PreviewSection

A block a detector adds to an item's preview.

```ts snippet
export type PreviewSection =
  | { type: "text"; title: string; text: string }
  | { type: "code"; title: string; code: string; language?: string }
  | { type: "keyValue"; title: string; rows: [string, string][] }
  | { type: "image"; title: string; image: ImageHandle }
  | { type: "link"; title: string; url: string };
```

## The yab object

The global `yab` is the extension's way to the app. Each part says when it works: some need a permission, and some work only in a run the person started (not in hints, detectors, previews or capture rules).

### yab.language

The app's language.

```ts snippet
readonly language: string;
```

### yab.t

This extension's string for `key` (app language → default locale → the key); `{name}` is replaced from `args`.

```ts snippet
t(key: string, args?: Record<string, string | number | boolean>): string;
```

### yab.preferences

This extension's preferences by id. A `folder` preference is an absolute path string (`~` already
expanded; a manifest default shows here too; "" when cleared). `yab.files.read` and `exists` may read inside
a folder only after the person chose it in Settings (a default alone grants nothing), never write.
A `secret` preference is never here: read it with `yab.secrets.get`.

```ts snippet
readonly preferences: Record<string, unknown>;
```

### yab.secrets

#### yab.secrets.get

The value of this extension's own `secret` preference `id`, or null when it has none or `id` is not a
declared secret. Needs no permission and works in every call. Never log it or put it in a result.

```ts snippet
get(id: string): string | null;
```

### yab.storage

A small store kept between calls (JSON values, 1 MB in all).

#### yab.storage.get

```ts snippet
get(key: string): unknown;
```

#### yab.storage.set

Throws when the store would pass 1 MB.

```ts snippet
set(key: string, value: unknown): void;
```

#### yab.storage.remove

```ts snippet
remove(key: string): void;
```

### yab.image

#### yab.image.info

```ts snippet
info(image: ImageHandle): { width: number; height: number; uti: string };
```

#### yab.image.convert

Rejects with code "unavailable" when the Mac cannot write the format (WebP on macOS 26).

```ts snippet
convert(image: ImageHandle, options: { format: "jpeg" | "png" | "webp" | "heic"; quality?: number; maxSize?: number }): Promise<ImageHandle>;
```

#### yab.image.resize

```ts snippet
resize(image: ImageHandle, options: { scale?: number; width?: number; height?: number }): Promise<ImageHandle>;
```

#### yab.image.fromBytes

```ts snippet
fromBytes(bytes: Uint8Array, uti?: string): ImageHandle;
```

### yab.vision

#### yab.vision.ocr

Recognized text, lines joined with "\n" (Turkish and English).

```ts snippet
ocr(image: ImageHandle): Promise<string>;
```

#### yab.vision.removeBackground

The image's foreground subject(s) cut out onto a transparent background (PNG with alpha), same size.
Rejects with code `unavailable` ("no subject found") when Vision finds no subject.

```ts snippet
removeBackground(image: ImageHandle): Promise<ImageHandle>;
```

#### yab.vision.readCodes

QR codes and barcodes found in the image.

```ts snippet
readCodes(image: ImageHandle): Promise<string[]>;
```

### yab.qr

#### yab.qr.generate

```ts snippet
generate(text: string, options?: { size?: number }): ImageHandle;
```

### yab.files

#### yab.files.workDir

This call's work folder; made on first use and removed when the call ends, unless it returns files.

```ts snippet
readonly workDir: string;
```

#### yab.files.write

Writes a file in the work folder and returns its path. `/` and `:` in the name become `-`;
`..`, an empty name and one over 200 characters throw with code "badResult". An image handle
is written as PNG.

```ts snippet
write(name: string, data: string | Uint8Array | ImageHandle): string;
```

#### yab.files.read

Reads a file from the work folder, one of the item's own `files`, or inside a folder the person chose in a
`folder` preference (links that lead out of it are refused); any other path throws "badResult".

```ts snippet
read(path: string): Uint8Array;
```

#### yab.files.exists

Whether a file exists in those places; false for any other path.

```ts snippet
exists(path: string): boolean;
```

### yab.http

#### yab.http.fetch

Fetches a URL; needs the `network` permission and only reaches the manifest's `network.domains`
(a host equals a domain or ends with ".domain"; redirects are held to the same list). Rejects with
"permissionDenied" (host not allowed), "networkError" (failed, redirected outside the domains, or a text
body over 10 MB without `toFile`) or "cancelled". Works only in a run the person started.
Header names in the response are lowercased. With `toFile` the body streams into the work folder and
`file` is its path (`true` names it after the URL's last path part, or "download"); a non-2xx answer is
returned as `text` instead.

```ts snippet
fetch(url: string, init?: HttpInit): Promise<HttpResponse>;
```

### yab.exec

Runs a tool from the manifest's `requires.tools`; needs the `exec` permission and works only in a run
the person started. No shell is involved: each argument reaches the tool as it is, so quoting,
`;`, `$(…)` and `*` mean nothing special. The tool runs in `yab.files.workDir` with only PATH
(the folders tools are looked for in, then /usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin), HOME, TMPDIR, USER and LANG
set. Resolves once it has exited and closed its output. Rejects with "permissionDenied" (no `exec`
permission, or the tool is not in `requires.tools`), "toolMissing" (not installed; the message says how
to install it), "badResult" (`args` is not an array of strings) or "cancelled". Cancelling the call or
aborting `signal` sends SIGTERM to the tool and everything it started, and SIGKILL two seconds later.

```ts snippet
exec(tool: string, args: string[], options?: ExecOptions): Promise<ExecResult>;
```

### yab.notify

Shows a calm notice titled with the extension's name. Works only in a run the person started (throws
"permissionDenied" in hints, detectors, previews and capture rules); needs no permission. The message is
cut to 200 characters, and an extension gets at most one notice every 3 seconds: more are dropped
without an error. Returns at once; the app shows it.

```ts snippet
notify(message: string): void;
```

### yab.open

Opens a web link in the default browser. Only http and https links open; any other throws "badResult".
Works only in a run the person started (throws "permissionDenied" in hints, detectors, previews and
capture rules); needs no permission. Returns at once; the app opens it.

```ts snippet
open(url: string): void;
```

### yab.history

#### yab.history.recent

The newest clipboard items, newest first. Needs the "history" permission and works only in a run the
person started or a job: rules, detectors and previews reject with "permissionDenied", as does an
extension without the permission (the message in the app's language). `limit` is 1 to 50 (20 when left
out; larger values are cut to 50). Items arrive trimmed: a text and an item's HTML are cut to 64 KB, and
an image carries only its width and height, never its pixels. Concealed copies are not in history.

```ts snippet
recent(limit?: number): Promise<HistoryItem[]>;
```

#### yab.history.search

The same, for items matching `query` (the search the panel uses). Same permission, limit and trimming.

```ts snippet
search(query: string, limit?: number): Promise<HistoryItem[]>;
```

### yab.ai

#### yab.ai.generate

Answers `prompt` with Apple's on-device model (Apple Intelligence); nothing leaves the Mac. Works only in
a run the person started or a job: hints, detectors, previews and capture rules reject with
"permissionDenied". Needs no permission. The prompt is cut to 32 000 characters, but the model reads far
less (a few thousand words): shorten long texts first.
Rejects with "unavailable" when the model cannot run, the message (in the app's language) saying what to
do: this Mac can't run Apple Intelligence, it is turned off in System Settings, or it is still getting
ready. It rejects with "unavailable" too, again in the app's language, when the text is too long for the
model, the model won't answer it, the language isn't supported yet, or the model is busy; a cancelled
call rejects with "cancelled". Transforming the person's own text (summarizing, rewriting) is not
refused for what the text contains.

```ts snippet
generate(prompt: string, options?: AIOptions): Promise<string>;
```

### yab.translate

Translates `text` on the Mac with Apple Translation into `to`, a BCP-47 code ("tr", "en", "zh-Hans").
`from` is the text's language; left out, it is recognized. A text already in `to` comes back as it is,
with `from` set, so compare `from` with `to` to tell. The text is cut to 32 000 characters. Works only in a
run the person started or a job (hints, detectors, previews and capture rules reject with
"permissionDenied"); needs no permission. Rejects with "badResult" for a missing text or language code,
"cancelled" when the call is cancelled, and "unavailable", the message in the app's language, when:
the pair's language pack isn't downloaded (yabbistir also offers to download it), the pair can't be
translated on this Mac, the text's language can't be told, or the translation otherwise fails.

```ts snippet
translate(text: string, options: { to: string; from?: string }): Promise<TranslationResult>;
```

### yab.job

#### yab.job.progress

Reports how far a job is, for its card. `fraction` 0–1 with numbers as the message
("18.4 / 43.7 MB · 1 min left"), or null when it cannot be told, with a state word
("Merging"). Throws with code "badResult" for anything else.

```ts snippet
progress(fraction: number | null, message?: string): void;
```

## Types used by yab

### HistoryItem

An item as `yab.history` returns it: images have their size only.

```ts snippet
export type HistoryItem = Omit<Item, "image"> & {
  image?: { width: number; height: number };
  /** True when the text or HTML was cut to 64 KB; absent otherwise. */
  readonly truncated?: boolean;
};
```

### AIOptions

`yab.ai.generate`'s options. Left out, each is the model's own default.

```ts snippet
export interface AIOptions {
  /** The model's role and rules for this answer ("Answer in one sentence."). Cut to 32 000 characters. */
  instructions?: string;
  /** 0 is the most predictable, 2 the most varied; values outside are held to 0–2. */
  temperature?: number;
  /** The longest answer, in tokens; values outside are held to 1–2048. */
  maxTokens?: number;
}
```

### TranslationResult

What `yab.translate` resolves with.

```ts snippet
export interface TranslationResult {
  text: string;
  /** The source language (BCP-47): the one given, or the one recognized. */
  from: string;
}
```

### HttpInit

```ts snippet
export interface HttpInit {
  method?: string;
  headers?: Record<string, string>;
  body?: string | Uint8Array;
  toFile?: boolean | string;
  /** Aborting it cancels the request; the promise rejects with code "cancelled". */
  signal?: AbortSignal;
}
```

### HttpResponse

```ts snippet
export interface HttpResponse {
  status: number;
  headers: Record<string, string>;
  text?: string;
  file?: string;
}
```

### ExecOptions

```ts snippet
export interface ExecOptions {
  /** Hears each line the tool writes, without its newline (empty lines are skipped), in order for each stream; bad UTF-8 bytes become "\uFFFD". */
  onLine?: (line: string, stream: "stdout" | "stderr") => void;
  /** Aborting it stops the tool and everything it started; the promise rejects with code "cancelled". */
  signal?: AbortSignal;
  /** Written to the tool's standard input, which is then closed. Without it, standard input is empty. */
  input?: string;
}
```

### ExecResult

```ts snippet
export interface ExecResult {
  /** The tool's exit code; 128 + the signal's number when a signal ended it. A non-zero code does not reject: judge it yourself. */
  exitCode: number;
  /** The last 64 KB the tool wrote to standard output. */
  stdout: string;
  /** The last 64 KB the tool wrote to standard error. */
  stderr: string;
}
```

## Errors

Every code, with its cause and fix, is in [errors](errors.md#runtime-errors).

### ExtensionErrorCode

Why a call failed. A `yab` function that throws, or a `yab` promise that rejects, gives an Error with one in `code`.

```ts snippet
export type ExtensionErrorCode =
  | "script"
  | "syntax"
  | "timeout"
  | "notFound"
  | "badResult"
  | "unavailable"
  | "unsupported"
  | "interrupted"
  | "permissionDenied"
  | "toolMissing"
  | "cancelled"
  | "networkError";
```

### YabError

What `yab` throws and rejects with: test `e.code`, e.g. `e.code === "cancelled"` once the person
cancelled the job. An error you throw yourself with a `code` from this list keeps it.

```ts snippet
export interface YabError extends Error {
  readonly code: ExtensionErrorCode;
}
```

## Globals

Besides `yab`, these web standards are there. Anything else a browser or Node has is not: see [errors](errors.md#node-builtins).

### console

```ts snippet
const console: { log(...values: unknown[]): void; info(...values: unknown[]): void; warn(...values: unknown[]): void; error(...values: unknown[]): void; debug(...values: unknown[]): void };
```

### setTimeout

```ts snippet

```

### fetch

Web-compatible and held to the same rules as `yab.http.fetch`; bodies up to 10 MB.


### URLSearchParams

```ts snippet
class URLSearchParams implements Iterable<[string, string]> {
  constructor(init?: string | Record<string, string> | [string, string][] | URLSearchParams);
  append(name: string, value: string): void;
  delete(name: string): void;
  get(name: string): string | null;
  getAll(name: string): string[];
  has(name: string): boolean;
  set(name: string, value: string): void;
  sort(): void;
  forEach(callback: (value: string, key: string, parent: URLSearchParams) => void): void;
  keys(): IterableIterator<string>;
  values(): IterableIterator<string>;
```
