```ts snippet
}
```

### AbortEvent

```ts snippet
interface AbortEvent {
  readonly type: "abort";
  readonly target: AbortSignal;
  readonly currentTarget: AbortSignal;
}
```

### AbortSignal

```ts snippet
class AbortSignal {
  private constructor();
  readonly aborted: boolean;
  /** What `abort` was given: an Error named "AbortError" by default, "TimeoutError" from `timeout`. */
  readonly reason: unknown;
  onabort: ((this: AbortSignal, event: AbortEvent) => void) | null;
  /** Each listener runs once, when the signal aborts; one added afterwards never runs. */
  addEventListener(type: "abort", listener: (this: AbortSignal, event: AbortEvent) => void): void;
  removeEventListener(type: "abort", listener: (this: AbortSignal, event: AbortEvent) => void): void;
  /** Throws `reason` once aborted. */
  throwIfAborted(): void;
  /** A signal that aborts after `ms` milliseconds. */
  static timeout(ms: number): AbortSignal;
}
```

### AbortController

```ts snippet
class AbortController {
  readonly signal: AbortSignal;
  /** Aborts the signal; only the first call counts. */
  abort(reason?: unknown): void;
}
```

```ts snippet
  pathname: string;
  search: string;

  readonly searchParams: URLSearchParams;
  readonly href: string;
  toString(): string;
  toJSON(): string;
}
```


================================================================================
File: docs/permissions.md
================================================================================

# Permissions

An extension starts with no permissions. Most need none: everything below works without asking.

- Reading the item it is given, and returning a result.
- Strings, preferences, secrets (`yab.secrets.get`) and its own small store (`yab.storage`).
- Files in the call's work folder (`yab.files`), and reading a folder the person chose in a `folder` preference.
- Images and Vision (`yab.image`, `yab.vision`, `yab.qr`).
- On-device AI (`yab.ai.generate`) and translation (`yab.translate`): the data never leaves the Mac.
- Notices (`yab.notify`) and opening a web link in the browser (`yab.open`).

Four things need a permission, listed in the manifest's `permissions`. Before the extension is installed, the person sees each one in a plain sentence and decides. An update that asks for a new permission waits until the person approves it. The app checks every call: a call the manifest does not allow fails with [`permissionDenied`](errors.md#permissiondenied).

| Permission | What it allows | What the person reads |
|---|---|---|
| [`network`](#network) | Reaching the internet, from a run the person started | "Can reach: example.com, api.example.com" or "Can reach any website" |
| [`exec`](#exec) | Running the programs listed in `requires.tools` | "Can run these programs on your Mac: yt-dlp, ffmpeg. They can read and write your files and reach the internet." |
| [`capture`](#capture) | Seeing each new copy, to run capture rules | "Can see everything you copy" |
| [`history`](#history) | Reading earlier copies | "Can read your whole history" |

**Ask for as little as you can.** Every permission is a sentence the person has to accept and a reason a reviewer reads your code more closely. List the hosts you need rather than any host, run one program rather than a shell, and prefer `yab.ai` and `yab.translate` to a web service when they can do the job. Each permission you keep needs a reason in the pull request and in the README.

## network

```json
{
  "permissions": ["network"],
  "network": { "domains": ["api.example.com"] }
}
```

- `yab.http.fetch(url, init)` and the web `fetch` both work, held to the same rules.
- Only in a run the person started (an action or a job). Hints, detectors, previews and capture rules get `permissionDenied`.
- Only to the listed hosts: a host matches a domain when it is the domain or ends with `.` and the domain, so `example.com` covers `www.example.com`. Redirects must stay inside the list. Leaving the list empty, or leaving `network` out, allows any host, and the consent sentence says "Can reach any website".
- `http` and `https` only. Response header names arrive lowercased. A text body over 10 MB fails unless it is streamed to a file with `toFile`.
- Failures reject with `networkError`, a host outside the list with `permissionDenied`, a cancelled job with `cancelled`.
- No cookies are kept between requests.

Network use must serve what the person asked for. Sending the item, or anything about the person, anywhere else is a data leak ([review checklist](review-checklist.md#data)).

See [Call an API with a key](recipes/call-an-api-with-a-key.md).

## exec

```json
{
  "permissions": ["exec"],
  "requires": {
    "tools": [{ "name": "yt-dlp", "install": "brew install yt-dlp" }]
  }
}
```

- `yab.exec(tool, args, options)` runs a program by name, and only one listed in `requires.tools`. Any other name is `permissionDenied`.
- The program is looked for in `/opt/homebrew/bin`, then `/usr/local/bin`, then the system's folders. If it is not installed, the call fails with `toolMissing` and a message that says how to install it, and Settings shows the `install` command for the person to copy.
- **No shell.** `args` is a list of strings, and each reaches the program as it is: quotes, `;`, `$(…)` and `*` mean nothing special. Never run a shell (`sh -c …`) to get around that.
- The program runs in the call's work folder (`yab.files.workDir`) with only `PATH`, `HOME`, `TMPDIR`, `USER` and `LANG` set. Its exit code comes back in `exitCode` and is not an error by itself: check it. `onLine` hears its output line by line; `input` is written to its standard input.
- Only in a run the person started. Cancelling the job, or aborting `signal`, stops the program and everything it started.

The program can do anything the person can, so a reviewer checks every argument. **Arguments are fixed or checked by the extension.** Put anything that comes from the item after `--`, so a link such as `--exec=…` can never be read as an option, and never pass options that make the program run other programs. See the [review checklist](review-checklist.md#exec) and [Download with yt-dlp](recipes/download-with-yt-dlp.md).

## capture

```json
{
  "permissions": ["capture"]
}
```

Needed by `contributes.captureRules`, and only for them. A rule sees each new copy's text or URL before it is stored. Rules never reach the network or run programs; see [Capture rules](capture-rules.md). The person can turn each rule off in Settings.

## history

```json
{
  "permissions": ["history"]
}
```

- `yab.history.recent(limit)` returns the newest items, newest first; `yab.history.search(query, limit)` returns those that match a search, the way the panel searches. `limit` is 1 to 50, and 20 when left out.
- Only in an action or a job. Detectors, previews and capture rules get `permissionDenied`.
- Items arrive trimmed: text and HTML are cut to 64 KB, and such an item has `truncated: true`. An image has only its `width` and `height`, never its pixels. Concealed copies, such as passwords, are never in history.

```ts
import type { Actions } from "@yabbistir/api";

export const actions: Actions = {
  joinRecent: {
    async run() {
      const items = await yab.history.recent(5);
      const texts = items.filter((item) => item.kind === "text" && !item.truncated).map((item) => item.text ?? "");
      if (texts.length === 0) return { none: true, message: yab.t("nothingRecent") };
      return { text: texts.join("\n") };
    },
  },
};
```

## Secrets and folders

Neither needs a permission, but both are preferences the person fills in Settings:

- A **`secret`** preference (an API key) is kept in the Keychain. Only `yab.secrets.get(id)` reads it, and it never appears in `yab.preferences`. Never log it or put it in a result.
- A **`folder`** preference holds an absolute path. `yab.files.read` and `yab.files.exists` may read inside it once the person has chosen it in Settings; a default alone grants nothing. Nothing can be written there: results are files in the work folder, and the app moves them.

## How the person sees it

- At install, from a file or a folder (and from the Store, coming in yabbistir 0.2.0), the permissions are listed and nothing happens until the person allows them. Extensions installed from a file or a folder are marked as not signed.
- Settings → Extensions shows each extension's permissions, preferences and source (Built-in, Local or Development, and Store from yabbistir 0.2.0), and has a switch that turns all third-party extensions off.
- A development extension linked with `npm run dev` asks for its permissions too: approve them in Settings → Extensions.


================================================================================
File: docs/errors.md
================================================================================

# Errors

Errors come from three places:

- **The validator** (`npm run validate`, and `npm run build` after it compiles): problems in the manifest, the locale files and the folder. Each has a code; [Validator messages](#validator-messages).
- **The build** (`npm run build`, `npm run dev`): code that cannot be bundled for JavaScriptCore; [Build errors](#build-errors).
- **The runtime** (the app, and the fake host in tests): a `yab` call or an extension call that failed, with a `code`; [Runtime errors](#runtime-errors).

## Reading the validator

`npm run validate -- <id>` prints one line per problem:

```text
extensions/dev.yourname.tool/manifest.json: contributes.actions[0].output: "txt" is not an output (expected text, html, image, link, file, files, none) → fix: Use one of: text, html, image, link, file, files, none.
```

That is the file, the field (as a path into the JSON), the message, what was expected, and a fix. A warning says `warning:` before its message. The command exits with 1 when there is any error, and with 0 for warnings alone. A clean extension prints `extensions/<id>: ok`.

`npm run build -- <id>` compiles `index.js` into `dist/<id>/`, checks that folder with the same rules, and packs nothing if there is an error. When that build is newer than everything in `extensions/<id>/` except `tests/`, `npm run validate` checks the build, `index.js` included, and names each issue at its source file; a clean result reads `extensions/<id>: ok, with its build in dist/<id>`. Without a build, or once the source has changed since, it checks the source folder and ends with `note: not built yet (or out of date): run npm run build -- <id> to check index.js too`.

### The store is stricter than the app

The validator runs the app's own checks, with the app's messages, and then the store's. So a manifest the app would load can still fail here:

- Fields the schema does not know are errors ([`unknownField`](#unknownfield)); the app ignores them.
- The schema's own limits are checked ([`schemaMismatch`](#schemamismatch)): option ids must be plain, `null` is not allowed in optional fields, `version` must use ASCII digits, and an action with `"input": "none"` still lists non-empty `kinds` if it has `accepts`.
- `accepts.pattern` may use only what the store can verify ([`invalidPattern`](#invalidpattern)).
- A license, README.md, CHANGELOG.md and a complete `locales/en.json` are required.
- The folder holds regular files and folders only ([`notARegularFile`](#notaregularfile)).

## Validator messages

The quoted text is the message; `<…>` stands for what the validator fills in.

### `manifestMissing`

`manifest.json is missing`. There is no `manifest.json` at the folder's root. **Fix:** add it; `npm run new` makes one.

### `manifestNotObject`

`manifest.json is not a JSON object`. The file is not valid JSON, or holds something other than an object. **Fix:** check commas, quotes and brackets; a trailing comma or a comment is not JSON.

### `manifestUnreadable`

`"<field>" must be <a string, true or false, a whole number, a list, an object>`, or `<field> must hold only text`. A field has the wrong type, such as `"hint": "yes"`, `"priority": 1.5` or `"minAppVersion": 2`. It is reported only once every other check passes. **Fix:** write the type the [manifest reference](manifest.md) gives.

### `missingField`

`"<field>" is missing`. A required field is not there. `apiVersion` gets this message when it is missing or not a number (`"1"` is a string). **Fix:** add the field; see the [manifest reference](manifest.md).

### `notAString`

`"<field>" must be a non-empty string`. A required text field is empty or not text. **Fix:** give it a value in quotes.

### `invalidID`

`"<id>" is not a reverse-domain id`. The id is not lowercase letters, digits and dashes in dot-separated parts, with at least two parts. **Fix:** use something like `dev.yourname.tool`, and rename the folder to match.

### `idFolderMismatch`

`the id "<id>" does not match the folder name "<folder>"`. **Fix:** the folder under `extensions/` is named exactly the id; rename one of them.

### `invalidVersion`

`"<version>" is not semantic versioning`. **Fix:** write `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`, such as `"1.0.0"`, optionally with a `-beta.1` suffix.

### `unsupportedAPIVersion`

`API version <n> is not supported`. **Fix:** `"apiVersion": 1`.

### `defaultLocaleMissing`

`there is no locales/<language>.json for the default locale`. **Fix:** add the file, or set `defaultLocale` to a language you ship (`"en"`).

### `unknownLocaleKey`

`the key "<key>" is not in locales/<default locale>.json`. A manifest field names a string key the default locale's file lacks. If any locale file is broken, the app reads none, and every key is reported; fix [`localeUnreadable`](#localeunreadable) first. **Fix:** add the key to the file. A `keywords` key's value is a list of strings.

### `unknownCategory`

`"<category>" is not a category`. **Fix:** use `text`, `links`, `images`, `files`, `developer`, `media`, `ai` or `productivity`.

### `unknownPermission`

`"<permission>" is not a permission`. **Fix:** use `network`, `exec`, `capture` or `history` ([Permissions](permissions.md)). AI, translation and files need none.

### `captureRulesNeedCapture`

`captureRules need the capture permission`. **Fix:** add `"capture"` to `permissions`, or remove the rules.

### `networkNeedsDomains`

`"network" needs a list of domains`. `network` is there but has no `domains` list. **Fix:** `"network": { "domains": ["api.example.com"] }`. An empty list allows any host.

### `invalidDomain`

`"<domain>" is not a plain lowercase host name`. **Fix:** write the host only: `api.example.com`, not `https://api.example.com/v1` or `*.example.com`. A domain covers its subdomains already.

### `execNeedsTools`

`"exec" needs the tools the extension runs`. **Fix:** list them: `"requires": { "tools": [{ "name": "yt-dlp", "install": "brew install yt-dlp" }] }`.

### `toolsNeedExec`

`tools are listed but "exec" is not a permission`. **Fix:** add `"exec"` to `permissions`, or remove `requires`.

### `notAnObject`

`a tool must be an object`, `a preference must be an object`, `an action must be an object`, `a variant must be an object`, `a capture rule must be an object`, `a detector must be an object`, or `"accepts" must be an object`. **Fix:** write that entry as `{ … }` with its fields.

### `invalidToolName`

`"<name>" is not a usable tool name`. **Fix:** use the command's bare name (`ffmpeg`), never a path (`/opt/homebrew/bin/ffmpeg`) or arguments.

### `invalidMemberID`

`"<id>" is not a usable <action, variant, preference, capture rule, detector> id`. **Fix:** use only letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`.

### `duplicateID`

`the <action, variant, preference, capture rule, detector> id "<id>" is used twice`. **Fix:** give each its own id within its list.

### `unknownPreferenceType`

`"<type>" is not a preference type`. **Fix:** use `text`, `toggle`, `choice`, `secret` or `folder`.

### `secretDefault`

`a secret cannot have a default`. **Fix:** remove `default`; the person types the secret in Settings.

### `folderDefault`

`a folder default must start with "~"`. **Fix:** write it as `"~/Downloads"`, or leave it out.

### `choiceNeedsOptions`

`a choice needs options`. **Fix:** add `"options": [{ "id": "short", "title": "format.short" }, …]`.

### `unknownInput`

`"<input>" is not an input`. **Fix:** `"item"` for a transform, `"none"` for a generator.

### `unknownOutput`

`"<output>" is not an output`. **Fix:** use `text`, `html`, `image`, `link`, `file`, `files` or `none` ([Results](results-and-targets.md)).

### `unknownTarget`

`"<target>" is not a target`. **Fix:** use `finder`, `terminal`, `browser`, `editor` or `other`.

### `targetsOnlyNeedsTargets`

`"targetsOnly" needs at least one entry in "targets"`. **Fix:** add `"targets": ["finder"]`, or remove `targetsOnly`.

### `acceptsMissing`

`an action that takes an item needs "accepts"`, `a capture rule needs "accepts"`, or `a detector needs "accepts"`. **Fix:** add `"accepts": { "kinds": ["text"] }`, narrowed with a `pattern` where it helps.

### `kindsEmpty`

`"kinds" is empty`. **Fix:** list at least one of `text`, `code`, `link`, `color`, `image`, `file`.

### `unknownKind`

`"<kind>" is not a kind`. **Fix:** use `text`, `code`, `link`, `color`, `image` or `file`. A URL is a `link`.

### `invalidPattern`

Either `"<pattern>" is not a valid regular expression`, or `the store validator cannot verify <construct> in "<pattern>"`.

`accepts.pattern` is an ICU regular expression, the kind macOS uses, not a JavaScript one. They differ: `(?i)` works in ICU, while a bare `{` or `[^]` does not.

The second message means the pattern uses something the store cannot check against the app, so it refuses it rather than risk a pattern the app rejects. That covers `\N{…}` character names and most `\p{Name=Value}` properties.

**Fix:** use the constructs listed in [Patterns](concepts.md#patterns): character classes such as `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`, `\d`, `\s`, `\w`, anchors, groups, alternation, `{m,n}`, look-around, and `\p{L}`, `\p{Lu}` or a script such as `\p{Latin}`. Escape a literal `{` as `\{`, and write `^…$` to match the whole text.

### `captureRuleTags`

A warning: `capture rules never see tags; this rule would never run`. A rule's `accepts` lists `tags`, but rules run before detectors tag anything, so it would never match. **Fix:** remove `tags`; filter on `kinds` and `pattern`.

### `indexMissing`

`index.js is missing`. A built folder has no `index.js`, or a source folder has neither `src/index.ts` nor `src/index.js`. **Fix:** add `src/index.ts` and run `npm run build -- <id>`.

### `licenseNotAllowed`

`"<license>" is not a license the store accepts`. **Fix:** use one of `MIT`, `Apache-2.0`, `BSD-2-Clause`, `BSD-3-Clause`, `ISC` or `MPL-2.0`; MIT is the usual choice.

### `readmeMissing`

`README.md is missing`. **Fix:** add one: what the extension does, an example, and why it needs each permission.

### `changelogMissing`

`CHANGELOG.md is missing`. **Fix:** add one with a `## <version>` section per version, newest first.

### `enLocaleMissing`

`locales/en.json is missing`. Every extension in the store ships English. **Fix:** add `locales/en.json` with every key.

### `enLocaleKeyMissing`

`the key "<key>" is not in locales/en.json`. **Fix:** add the key to `locales/en.json`.

### `localeUnreadable`

`locales/<language>.json is not a JSON object`. One broken locale file and the app reads no locale at all, so the extension would show bare keys. **Fix:** make the file valid JSON: one object of keys and strings (lists for keywords).

### `unknownField`

`"<name>" is not a manifest field here`. A misspelled or invented field, such as `"permision"` or `"jsAccepts"`. **Fix:** remove it, or correct the spelling against the [manifest reference](manifest.md).

### `schemaMismatch`

A schema rule the app's own checks do not cover, such as `"Not Plain" does not have the expected form` (an option id), `must not be empty`, or `must be a string, not null`. **Fix:** compare the field with the [manifest reference](manifest.md): leave optional fields out rather than setting them to `null`.

### `notARegularFile`

`it is a symbolic link, and an extension holds only regular files and folders`, or `it is not a regular file`. The build copies files into the package, and a link would bring whatever it points at, so the store refuses links, pipes and devices anywhere in the extension's folder; `node_modules` is left to npm. `npm run build` stops on it before it copies anything. **Fix:** put a copy of the file itself in the folder, or remove the link.

## Build errors

The build prefixes each message with `extensions/<id>:` and ends with `build failed: <id>`.

### Node builtins

```text
extensions/dev.yourname.tool: extensions/dev.yourname.tool/src/index.ts:1:16: "node:fs" is a Node.js module, and extensions do not run in Node. Use the `yab` API or a web standard instead (see docs/errors.md#node-builtins).
extensions/dev.yourname.tool: `process` is a Node.js global, and extensions do not run in Node. Use the `yab` API or a web standard instead (see docs/errors.md#node-builtins).
```

**Why.** Extensions run in JavaScriptCore inside yabbistir's helper process, not in Node. Node's modules (`fs`, `path`, `child_process`, `http`, `crypto`, …) and globals (`process`, `Buffer`, `require`, `global`, `__dirname`, `__filename`) do not exist there, and code that reaches for them would fail at run time. The build stops it earlier:

- Any import of a Node module, with or without `node:`, is refused. That includes **npm packages whose names are Node's**, such as `events`, `util`, `url`, `buffer`, `assert`, `path`, `punycode` and `string_decoder`, even when installed from npm: the build cannot tell them apart.
- Any use of `process`, `Buffer`, `require`, `global`, `__dirname` or `__filename` that the code does not define itself is refused. That includes guards such as `typeof process !== "undefined"` or `typeof require === "function"` inside a bundled library.
- An import that is never used is dropped before the check, so it does not fail.

**What to use instead:**

| Node | In an extension |
|---|---|
| `fs` | `yab.files.write`, `read` and `exists` (the call's work folder, the item's files, chosen folders) |
| `path` | String operations on `/`-separated paths, or `new URL(…)` |
| `child_process` | `yab.exec` with the `exec` permission ([Permissions](permissions.md#exec)) |
| `http`, `https`, `net` | `fetch` or `yab.http.fetch` with the `network` permission |
| `crypto` | `crypto.getRandomValues`, `crypto.randomUUID`, or a pure-JavaScript library |
| `Buffer` | `Uint8Array`, `TextEncoder`, `TextDecoder`, `atob`, `btoa` |
| `process.env`, `process.platform` | Preferences, secrets (`yab.secrets.get`), `yab.language`; it is always macOS |
| `url` | The global `URL` and `URLSearchParams` |
| `events`, `util` | A few lines of your own, or a library that does not import them |
| `setImmediate`, `process.nextTick` | `setTimeout(fn, 0)` or `await Promise.resolve()` |

For an npm package, choose one made for browsers without Node polyfills, or with no dependencies. If a library only works in Node, it does not work in an extension. `npm run typecheck` shows the same problem early: `process`, `Buffer` and `require` have no types here.

### Could not resolve

`extensions/<id>/src/index.ts:<line>:<column>: Could not resolve "<package>"`. The import names a package that is not installed, or a file that is not there. **Fix:** check the spelling, and import your own files with their `.ts` extension (`./parse.ts`). A library goes in a `package.json` in the extension's own folder, at an exact version; run `npm install` from the repository's root, which uses npm workspaces ([Testing](testing.md#libraries)).

### Other build messages

- `"<id>" is not an extension id`: pass the folder name under `extensions/`, such as `dev.yourname.tool`.
- `extensions/<id>: there is no such extension folder`: create it with `npm run new`, or check the id.
- `extensions/<id>/manifest.json: it is missing or is not valid JSON`: see [`manifestNotObject`](#manifestnotobject).
- `extensions/<id>/src/index.ts: it is missing`: add it; it exports `actions`, `detectors` and/or `captureRules`.
- A syntax error names the file, line and column: fix the code there.
- Validator lines after a successful compile: the built folder failed a check above; nothing was packed.

`npm run dev` refuses to touch `~/Library/Application Support/yabbistir/Extensions/<id>` when it is a real folder, an installed copy: `… is a real folder (an installed copy of <id>), so dev leaves it alone`. Remove that copy in Settings → Extensions, then run it again.

## Runtime errors

Every error a `yab` function throws or rejects with has a `code` ([`ExtensionErrorCode`](api.md#extensionerrorcode)), and so does a failed call into the extension. Test it as `error.code`. An `Error` you throw yourself with one of these codes keeps it; any other thrown error is `script`.

### `script`

The extension threw. **Cause:** your code, a failed check of your own, or a `yab` error you wrapped. **Fix:** for a real failure, throw an `Error` whose message a person can act on (`yab.t`). For an expected situation (no input, wrong shape), return `{ none: true, message }` instead: in an action, thrown errors count toward [turning the extension off](#turned-off-after-repeated-errors).

### `syntax`

`index.js` does not parse. Any load that fails, this or a top level that throws, is logged in the Development log as `index.js could not load: …`. **Fix:** run `npm run build` again; keep the top level to declarations, free of work that can throw.

### `timeout`

The call ran past its limit: 500 ms for a hint or a preview, 50 ms for `validate`, 200 ms for a capture rule, 10 seconds for an action. **Fix:** make it a [job](jobs.md) if it is slow by nature; otherwise do less, or narrow `accepts` so it runs less often.

### `notFound`

The app called an action, detector or rule the code does not export. **Fix:** the ids in the manifest and the keys of `actions`, `detectors` and `captureRules` in `src/index.ts` must match exactly.

### `badResult`

What the call returned is not a result the app accepts, or a `yab` call got arguments it cannot use. Examples: `run` returned a string instead of `{ text }`, a file result outside `yab.files.workDir`, a preview section of an unknown `type`, `yab.exec` with arguments that are not strings, `yab.files.write` with `..` in the name, `yab.job.progress` with a fraction that is not a number. The app logs the reason to the Development log. **Fix:** return one of the [result shapes](results-and-targets.md); the fake host reports the same reason in tests.

### `unavailable`

What was asked for cannot be done on this Mac right now: Apple Intelligence is off or not ready, a translation language pack is missing, WebP cannot be written, Vision found no subject, the helper is restarting, or the extension was turned off. The message says which, in the app's language. **Fix:** let it through so the person sees it; there is nothing to retry in code.

### `unsupported`

The extension needs something this version of the app does not offer. **Fix:** set `minAppVersion` to the version that has it.

### `interrupted`

Cut short by something else: another call's timeout restarted the helper, or the helper stopped. It never counts against the extension. **Fix:** nothing; the person can try again.

### `permissionDenied`

A call the manifest does not allow, or that is not allowed in this kind of call: the network without `network`, a host outside `network.domains`, a tool not in `requires.tools`, `yab.history` without `history`, or any effect (network, programs, notices, opening links, AI, translation, history) in a hint, detector, preview or capture rule. **Fix:** add the permission or the domain if the extension really needs it, and move effects into an action the person starts.

### `toolMissing`

A tool from `requires.tools` is not installed. The message says how to install it (the manifest's `install`), and Settings shows that command. **Fix:** let it through; in tests, a tool missing from the fake host's `exec` table gives this error.

### `cancelled`

The person cancelled the job, or `signal` was aborted. Every pending `yab` promise rejects with it. **Fix:** let it through; never catch it and carry on.

### `networkError`

A request failed: no connection, a redirect outside `network.domains`, or a text body over 10 MB without `toFile`. **Fix:** let it through, or catch it and throw a clearer message (keep `cancelled` untouched); stream large bodies with `toFile`.

## Turned off after repeated errors

Three failures in a row turn an extension off; Settings shows it as off and a notice says so. A success resets the count. Not every failure counts:

- **Never counted:** `cancelled`, `interrupted`, `toolMissing`, `networkError`, `permissionDenied`.
- **In a job,** only a broken extension counts: `badResult`, `notFound`, `syntax`. A job's own thrown errors are reported to the person, not counted.
- **Everywhere else** (actions, hints, detectors, previews, rules), any other failure counts, `script` and `timeout` included.
- A load that fails (`index.js could not load`) counts too.

The person turns it back on in Settings. Read Settings → Extensions → Development → Log to see why.

## Test failures

Messages the fake host gives in `npm test`:

- `<host>: the request failed (no fake response for GET <url>)` (`networkError`): the code made a request the test did not answer. Add it to `http`, with the whole URL.
- `<host> is not in the extension's domains` (`permissionDenied`): add the domain to `network.domains`, or fix the URL.
- `<tool> is not installed. Install it with: …` (`toolMissing`): add the tool to the fake host's `exec` table.
- `<tool> is not in the extension's required tools` (`permissionDenied`): add it to `requires.tools`.
- `the fake host has no AI answer; pass createFakeHost({ ai })` (`unavailable`), and the same for `translate` and `vision`.
- `run returned … ; expected {text}, {html, text}, …` (`badResult`): return a result shape.
- `… is not available in hints, detectors and previews` (`permissionDenied`): an effect in a call without effects.
- `ERR_UNSUPPORTED_TYPESCRIPT_SYNTAX`, or a TypeScript import that Node cannot load: use `import type` for `@yabbistir/api`, import your files with `.ts`, avoid `enum` and `namespace`, and use Node 22.18 or later ([Testing](testing.md)).


================================================================================
File: docs/jobs.md
================================================================================

# Jobs

A **job** is an action that takes a while: a download, a conversion, a summary of a long text. Add `"job": true` to the action in the manifest. The panel closes as soon as the person picks it, and a card under the menu bar icon shows the job's progress, with a button to cancel it. A job has no time limit; an action without `job` has 10 seconds.

```json
{ "id": "compress", "title": "compress.title", "keywords": "compress.keywords", "input": "item",
  "accepts": { "kinds": ["text", "code"] }, "output": "file", "job": true, "verb": "compress.verb", "failTitle": "compress.failed" }
```

- `verb` is the label in the ⇧ panel: "↵ Compress · ⌘C Compress and copy". Without it, a job says "Start".
- `failTitle` titles the card when the job fails: "Couldn't compress". A variant can have its own.
- At most three jobs run at once; more wait on the card as "Queued". Quitting the app cancels them.

## Progress

`yab.job.progress(fraction, message)` updates the card:

- With a `fraction` from 0 to 1, the card shows a bar and the message as numbers: `"18.4 / 43.7 MB · 1 min left"`.
- With `null`, the card shows an indeterminate bar and the message as a state word: `"Connecting"`, `"Merging"`.

Report when something changes, not on every line a program prints: once per whole percent, or twice a second at most, and state words when the phase changes. The card redraws calmly that way. Any other value for `fraction` throws `badResult`.

## Cancelling

When the person cancels, `ctx.signal` aborts, and every pending `yab` promise rejects with the code `cancelled`. Pass `ctx.signal` on to `yab.exec` and `yab.http.fetch` so the program or the download stops too, and let the `cancelled` error through: do not catch it and carry on. Whatever `run` returns after a cancel is dropped.

```ts
import type { Actions } from "@yabbistir/api";

export const actions: Actions = {
  compress: {
    async run(item, ctx) {
      const text = item?.text ?? "";
      if (text === "") return { none: true, message: yab.t("empty") };
      yab.job.progress(null, yab.t("compressing"));
      const input = yab.files.write("text.txt", text);
      // gzip -k writes text.txt.gz next to text.txt, in the work folder.
      const result = await yab.exec("gzip", ["-k", "-9", "--", input], { signal: ctx.signal });
      if (result.exitCode !== 0) throw new Error(yab.t("failed"));
      yab.job.progress(1, yab.t("done"));
      return { file: `${input}.gz` };
    },
  },
};
```

That job needs `"permissions": ["exec"]` and `"requires": { "tools": [{ "name": "gzip", "install": "It comes with macOS." }] }`.

A long loop of your own checks the signal now and then:

```ts snippet
for (const [index, line] of lines.entries()) {
  ctx.signal.throwIfAborted();
  out.push(convert(line));
  if (index % 1000 === 0) yab.job.progress(index / lines.length, yab.t("lines", { done: index, total: lines.length }));
}
```

## When it ends

- **Done:** if the app the job started for is still in front, the result is pasted. Otherwise it goes to the clipboard and the card says "Ready, ⌘V to paste". A file for Finder lands in the open folder ("Saved to Finder"). With the Stack open, the result joins the Stack. Every result joins history. If the person started it with ⌘C, the result goes to the clipboard.
- **Failed:** the card shows `failTitle` (or the action's title) and why. An `Error` you throw yourself shows its message, so write it for people, with `yab.t`. An error with a `yab` code shows the app's own wording: `networkError` "Couldn't connect", `toolMissing` "<tool> isn't installed", `permissionDenied` "Not allowed", `unavailable` "The extension isn't available right now", and the rest "Couldn't finish". To say something more specific, catch the error, and throw your own message, but never for `cancelled`:

```ts snippet
try {
  response = await yab.http.fetch(url, { signal: ctx.signal });
} catch (error) {
  if ((error as YabError).code === "cancelled") throw error;
  throw new Error(yab.t("serviceDown"));
}
```

A thrown error does not count against the extension in a job; only a broken result does (see [errors](errors.md#turned-off-after-repeated-errors)).

## Testing a job

The fake host records each progress report in `host.progress`, answers `yab.exec` from a table, and `host.cancel()` cancels like the card's button. See [Testing](testing.md#jobs-and-programs).

```js
const host = createFakeHost({ folder, exec: { gzip: (args, { host, workDir }) => {
  host.files.set(`${workDir}/text.txt.gz`, new Uint8Array([0x1f, 0x8b]));
  return { exitCode: 0, stdout: "", stderr: "" };
} } });
const result = await host.run(actions.compress, { text: "hello" });
assert.match(result.file, /text\.txt\.gz$/);
assert.deepEqual(host.progress.map((entry) => entry.fraction), [null, 1]);
```

The [job template](../templates/job) (`npm run new -- <id> --template job`) and [Download with yt-dlp](recipes/download-with-yt-dlp.md) are complete jobs.


================================================================================
File: docs/results-and-targets.md
================================================================================

# Results and targets

An action's `run` returns a **result**: plain data the app turns into a clipboard item. The app writes it to the clipboard, pastes it into the app the panel opened for, and adds it to history. An extension never writes the clipboard or sends keystrokes itself.

## Result shapes

| Manifest `output` | `run` returns | What the app does |
|---|---|---|
| `text` | `{ text }` | Pastes plain text. |
| `html` | `{ html, text }` | Writes both: apps that take rich text get the HTML, others the plain text. |
| `image` | `{ image }` | Pastes the image. The handle comes from the item, `yab.image`, `yab.vision`, `yab.qr` or `yab.image.fromBytes`. A copy is also kept as a file, so Finder can take it. |
| `link` | `{ link: { url, title? } }` | Pastes a link. |
| `file` | `{ file }` | A path in the call's work folder. The app moves the file into its own output folder, and it joins history as a file item. |
| `files` | `{ files: [...] }` | The same, for several files (at least one). |
| `none` | `{ none: true, message? }` | Pastes nothing. A non-empty `message` shows as a calm notice. |

Declare in `output` the shape `run` returns. Anything that is not one of these shapes fails the call with [`badResult`](errors.md#badresult), and the reason goes to the Development log.

```ts
import type { Actions } from "@yabbistir/api";

/** **bold** and _italic_ in copied Markdown, as rich text with the plain text beside it. */
function inlineMarkdown(text: string): { html: string; text: string } {
  const escaped = text.replace(/&/g, "&amp;").replace(/</g, "&lt;").replace(/>/g, "&gt;");
  const html = escaped.replace(/\*\*(.+?)\*\*/g, "<b>$1</b>").replace(/_(.+?)_/g, "<i>$1</i>");
  return { html, text: text.replace(/\*\*(.+?)\*\*/g, "$1").replace(/_(.+?)_/g, "$1") };
}

export const actions: Actions = {
  richText: {
    run(item) {
      return inlineMarkdown(item?.text ?? "");
    },
  },
  search: {
    run(item) {
      const query = (item?.text ?? "").trim();
      if (query === "") return { none: true, message: yab.t("empty") };
      return { link: { url: `https://example.com/search?q=${encodeURIComponent(query)}`, title: query } };
    },
  },
  qr: {
    run(item) {
      const text = item?.url ?? item?.text ?? "";
      if (text === "") return { none: true, message: yab.t("empty") };
      return { image: yab.qr.generate(text, { size: 512 }) };
    },
  },
};
```

## Files

A file result must be a file in the call's work folder, `yab.files.workDir`. Ways to put one there:

- `yab.files.write(name, data)` writes a string, bytes or an image (as PNG) and returns the path.
- `yab.http.fetch(url, { toFile: true })` streams a download there (`network` permission).
- A program run with `yab.exec` runs in that folder, so what it writes lands there (`exec` permission).

The work folder is made on first use and removed when the call ends, unless the result names files in it. The app then moves those files into its own output folder. Any path outside the work folder is refused. Read files with `yab.files.read`: the work folder, the item's own `files`, or a folder the person chose in a `folder` preference.

## Paste targets

`ctx.target` is the app the result is headed for, when known: its `bundleID`, `name` and a `kind`, one of `finder`, `terminal`, `browser`, `editor` or `other`. The manifest uses the kinds:

- `"targets": ["finder"]`: with Finder in front, the action leads the list.
- `"targetsOnly": true`: the action is offered only for those targets.

When the target is Finder, a `file` or `files` result lands in the open Finder folder as a file. Text and image results behave as they always do. See [Drop a file into Finder](recipes/drop-a-file-in-finder.md).

Use `ctx.target` to shape a result, not to decide whether to act: for example, a path quoted for a terminal and plain for an editor.

```ts
import type { Actions } from "@yabbistir/api";

export const actions: Actions = {
  path: {
    run(item, ctx) {
      const path = item?.files?.[0]?.path ?? "";
      if (path === "") return { none: true, message: yab.t("noFile") };
      const quoted = `'${path.replace(/'/g, `'\\''`)}'`;
      return { text: ctx.target?.kind === "terminal" ? quoted : path };
    },
  },
};
```

## How the person gets the result

- **↵** pastes the result into the target app. **⌘C** copies it instead.
- With the Stack open, a copied result joins the Stack.
- A [job](jobs.md) finishes later: if the target app is still in front, the result is pasted; otherwise it goes to the clipboard and a notice says "Ready, ⌘V to paste". A file for Finder lands in Finder.
- Every result joins history, like any other copy.

## Notices and links

Besides its result, a run the person started can:

- **Show a notice** with `yab.notify(message)`: a calm notice titled with the extension's name. The message is cut to 200 characters. The app shows at most one notice every 3 seconds per extension and drops the rest without an error; the helper also stops a flood at 5 notices in 10 seconds. Prefer `{ none: true, message }` when the message is the whole answer.
- **Open a web link** in the default browser with `yab.open(url)`; only `http` and `https` links open.

Neither needs a permission, and neither works in hints, detectors, previews or capture rules (`permissionDenied`). Both return at once.

## Generators and hints

A generator (`"input": "none"`) gets `null` for the item. With `"hint": true` it runs once its row is shown, and the value on the row is the value pasted; the next time, it runs again for a new value.

```ts
import type { Actions } from "@yabbistir/api";

export const actions: Actions = {
  timestamp: {
    run() {
      return { text: String(Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000)) };
    },
  },
};
```

A transform with `"hint": true` runs early on the selected item. Hints never run for jobs, `file` or `files` output, images, or text over 256 KB; those rows show their `subtitle` instead.

A hint that returns `{ none: true }` does not hide the action: it stays offered, and its row shows no preview. With a `message`, that message is the row's preview line, and picking the row shows it as a notice. So a hint can say "There is nothing to turn into a slug." before the person picks it.


================================================================================
File: docs/detectors-and-previews.md
================================================================================

# Detectors and previews

A **detector** recognizes a kind of content when it is copied, such as a JSON Web Token, an issue key or a Unix timestamp, and puts a **tag** on the item. The tag shows as a small grey chip on the item, actions can be offered only on tagged items, and the detector can add sections to the item's preview.

## The manifest

```json
{
  "contributes": {
    "detectors": [
      { "id": "timestamp", "tag": "tag", "accepts": { "kinds": ["text"], "pattern": "^[0-9]{10}$" },
        "validate": true, "preview": true }
    ]
  }
}
```

- `accepts` narrows the candidates without running any code: `kinds`, and a `pattern` searched for in the text or URL (write `^…$` to match the whole text). Make it as tight as you can.
- `"validate": true` calls `detectors[id].validate(item)` on each candidate. It returns `true` to keep the tag and `false` to drop it. It must answer at once, without a promise, in at most 50 ms. Return `false` for anything unexpected rather than throwing: a throw is a failure, and repeated failures turn the extension off. Without `validate`, the pattern alone decides.
- `"preview": true` calls `detectors[id].preview(item, ctx)` when the preview of a tagged item opens.
- `tag` is a locale key whose text is the chip: one short word, such as `JWT`.

Detectors run in the background when an item is copied. When a detector is new, or its extension has a new version, it also goes through the existing history once, in the background. Items whose text is over 256 KB are not looked at.

## Tags

A tagged item carries `"<extension id>:<detector id>"` in `item.tags`, for example `"dev.yourname.timestamp:timestamp"`. In a manifest, `accepts.tags` offers an action only on items with one of the tags. A tag of the extension's own detector can be written by its id alone:

```json
{ "id": "toDate", "title": "toDate.title", "keywords": "toDate.keywords", "input": "item",
  "accepts": { "kinds": ["text"], "tags": ["timestamp"] }, "output": "text" }
```

Another extension's tag is written in full: `"tags": ["dev.yabbistir.jwt:jwt"]`. Capture rules never see tags, because they run before any tag exists ([Capture rules](capture-rules.md)).

## Previews

`preview(item, ctx)` returns a list of sections, and the app draws them in the preview, in its own style:

| Section | Fields | For |
|---|---|---|
| `text` | `title`, `text` | A sentence or a paragraph. |
| `code` | `title`, `code`, `language?` | Formatted code; `language` such as `"json"`. |
| `keyValue` | `title`, `rows: [key, value][]` | Short facts. |
| `image` | `title`, `image` | An image handle, such as one from `yab.qr.generate`. |
| `link` | `title`, `url` | A link the person can open. |

A preview runs without effects, in at most 500 ms: no network, programs, notices, AI, translation or history. It can be `async`, but has nothing slow to wait for. Return `[]` when there is nothing to show. Use `ctx.language` to format dates and numbers.

```ts
import type { Detectors, Item, PreviewSection } from "@yabbistir/api";

const tenDigits = /^[0-9]{10}$/;

/** Seconds since 1970 between 2001 and 2286, which is what ten digits that look like a timestamp usually are. */
export function seconds(item: Item): number | null {
  const text = (item.text ?? "").trim();
  if (!tenDigits.test(text)) return null;
  const value = Number(text);
  return value >= 978_307_200 ? value : null;
}

function format(date: Date, language: string, timeZone?: string): string {
  try {
    return new Intl.DateTimeFormat(language, { dateStyle: "long", timeStyle: "medium", timeZone }).format(date);
  } catch {
    return date.toISOString();
  }
}

export const detectors: Detectors = {
  timestamp: {
    validate: (item) => seconds(item) !== null,
    preview(item, ctx): PreviewSection[] {
      const value = seconds(item);
      if (value === null) return [];
      const date = new Date(value * 1000);
      return [{
        type: "keyValue",
        title: yab.t("preview.title"),
        rows: [
          [yab.t("preview.local"), format(date, ctx.language)],
          ["UTC", format(date, ctx.language, "UTC")],
          ["ISO 8601", date.toISOString()],
        ],
      }];
    },
  },
};
```

## Testing

`host.validate(detectors.id, item)` resolves to `true` or `false`, and `host.preview(detectors.id, item)` to the sections. Both run without effects, as in the app, and the fake host checks that `validate` does not return a promise and that every section has a known `type`.

```js
assert.equal(await host.validate(detectors.timestamp, { text: "1767225600" }), true);
assert.equal(await host.validate(detectors.timestamp, { text: "12345" }), false);
const [section] = await host.preview(detectors.timestamp, { text: "1767225600" });
assert.deepEqual(section.rows[2], ["ISO 8601", "2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z"]);
```

The [detector template](../templates/detector) (`npm run new -- <id> --template detector`) is a working detector, the [Tag and preview](recipes/tag-and-preview.md) recipe adds an action on the tag, and [JWT](../extensions/dev.yabbistir.jwt) is a real one.


================================================================================
File: docs/capture-rules.md
================================================================================

# Capture rules

A **capture rule** sees each new copy before it reaches history and decides what happens to it: keep it, store a cleaned version instead, also put it in a category, or not store it at all. A rule that strips tracking parameters from copied links is the classic example.

Rules need the `capture` permission, which the person reads as "Can see everything you copy". Ask for it only when a rule is the extension's purpose.

## The manifest

```json
{
  "permissions": ["capture"],
  "contributes": {
    "captureRules": [
      { "id": "clean", "title": "clean.title", "description": "clean.description",
        "accepts": { "kinds": ["link", "text"], "pattern": "(?i)^\\s*https?://\\S+\\s*$" } }
    ]
  }
}
```

- `accepts` picks the copies the rule runs on, by `kinds` and an optional `pattern` (an ICU regular expression, searched for in the text or URL; `(?i)` makes it ignore case). The pattern is matched against the first 64 KB of the text; the rule itself gets the whole copy.
- **Rules see text and URLs only: no tags, no pixels.** Tags come from detectors, which run after the copy is stored, so `accepts.tags` on a rule would never match; the validator warns with [`captureRuleTags`](errors.md#captureruletags). Use `text`, `code` and `link` kinds.
- `title` and `description` appear in Settings, where the person can turn each rule off.

## The code

`captureRules[id].run(item, ctx)` returns one of:

| Return | Effect |
|---|---|
| `{ keep: true }`, or nothing | Store the copy as it is. |
| `{ replace: { text } }` or `{ replace: { url } }` | Store this plain text or link instead (not empty). Only for text, code and link copies. |
| `{ addToCategory: "Name" }` | Also put it in this category. The category must exist; case and accents are ignored, and an unknown name is ignored. |
| `{ ignore: true }` | Do not store it. The rules after this one do not run. |

```ts
import type { CaptureRules } from "@yabbistir/api";

const tracking = /^(utm_[a-z]+|fbclid|gclid)$/;

/** The link without tracking parameters, or null when it has none. */
export function clean(address: string): string | null {
  let url: URL;
  try {
    url = new URL(address.trim());
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
  const names = [...url.searchParams.keys()].filter((name) => tracking.test(name));
  if (names.length === 0) return null;
  for (const name of names) url.searchParams.delete(name);
  return url.href;
}

export const captureRules: CaptureRules = {
  clean: {
    run(item) {
      const cleaned = clean(item.url ?? item.text ?? "");
      if (cleaned === null) return { keep: true };
      return item.kind === "link" ? { replace: { url: cleaned } } : { replace: { text: cleaned } };
    },
  },
};
```

## The rules for rules

- **Fast and pure.** A rule has 200 ms. Past that, or if it throws, it is skipped and the copy is stored as it is; the Development log names the rule and the error's code, never the copy.
- **No effects.** No network, no programs, no history, no AI or translation, no notices, no opening links: these throw or reject with `permissionDenied`. `ctx.trigger` is `"capture"`.
- **Keep when unsure.** A rule that changes a copy the person did not expect is worse than one that does nothing.
- **In order.** Rules run one at a time, in the order the extensions are listed in Settings and then in manifest order. Each sees what the ones before it made of the copy.
- **Big copies pass.** A copy whose text or link is over 256 KB meets no rule. Concealed copies, such as passwords, never reach a rule.

## What the person sees

A replaced copy is stored in its clean form. If the clipboard still holds that same copy, the clean form is written there too, as plain text or a link, so the next ⌘V pastes it; rich formats are dropped. While the Stack is open, the clipboard is left alone and the clean form joins the Stack.

## Testing

`host.capture(captureRules.id, item)` runs a rule as the app does, without effects, and checks what it returns.

```js
assert.deepEqual(await host.capture(captureRules.clean, { kind: "link", url: "https://example.com/?id=7&utm_source=x" }),
  { replace: { url: "https://example.com/?id=7" } });
assert.deepEqual(await host.capture(captureRules.clean, { kind: "link", url: "https://example.com/" }), { keep: true });
```

The [capture-rule template](../templates/capture-rule) (`npm run new -- <id> --template capture-rule`), the [link-cleaning recipe](recipes/link-cleaning-rule.md) and [Link Cleaner](../extensions/dev.yabbistir.link-clean) are complete rules.


================================================================================
File: docs/localization.md
================================================================================

# Localization

yabbistir speaks English and Turkish, and an extension speaks the app's language through its locale files. Every extension ships English; other languages are welcome and optional.

## Locale files

`locales/<language>.json` is a flat JSON object from keys to strings. A `keywords` key holds a list of strings instead.

```json
{
  "name": "Slugify",
  "description": "Turns copied text into a URL slug.",
  "slugify.title": "Slugify",
  "slugify.keywords": ["slug", "slugify", "url"],
  "empty": "There is nothing to turn into a slug.",
  "count": "{n} slugs made"
}
```

- `locales/en.json` is required, and must hold every key the manifest uses.
- `defaultLocale` in the manifest is the fallback language; use `"en"`. Its file must hold every key the manifest uses too.
- Other languages may leave keys out: a missing string falls back to the default locale.
- Name keys after what they label: `slugify.title`, `slugify.keywords`, `download.fail`. Keys are never shown to anyone, unless one is missing everywhere.

A Turkish file for the same extension:

```json
{
  "name": "Slug",
  "description": "Kopyaladığın metni bir URL kısa adına çevirir.",
  "slugify.title": "Kısa ada çevir",
  "slugify.keywords": ["kısa ad", "slug", "url"],
  "empty": "Kısa ada çevrilecek bir şey yok."
}
```

## In the manifest

Every field a person reads holds a **key**, never the text: `name`, `description`, action `title`, `subtitle`, `keywords`, `verb` and `failTitle`, variant titles, detector `tag`, rule `title` and `description`, preference `title` and `confirm`, option `title`. The app looks each one up in the app's language.

## In code

`yab.t(key, args)` returns the string for `key` in the app's language, then in the default locale, then the key itself. `{name}` placeholders are filled from `args`; numbers and booleans become text.

```ts
import type { Actions } from "@yabbistir/api";

export const actions: Actions = {
  count: {
    run(item, ctx) {
      const words = (item?.text ?? "").split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean).length;
      const formatted = new Intl.NumberFormat(ctx.language).format(words);
      return { none: true, message: yab.t("count", { n: formatted }) };
    },
  },
};
```

- `ctx.language` and `yab.language` are the app's language, such as `"en"` or `"tr"`.
- Format numbers and dates with `Intl` and that language. `Intl` throws on a tag it does not know, so wrap it in `try` when the language comes from data.
- Keywords help people find the action in their own words; give each language its own, and add a few English ones to other languages, since people search in both.
- Write every message a person reads (results, notices, job progress, errors you throw) with `yab.t`.

## What the validator checks

- [`unknownLocaleKey`](errors.md#unknownlocalekey): a manifest key is missing from the default locale's file.
- [`enLocaleKeyMissing`](errors.md#enlocalekeymissing): a manifest key is missing from `locales/en.json`.
- [`enLocaleMissing`](errors.md#enlocalemissing): there is no `locales/en.json`.
- [`defaultLocaleMissing`](errors.md#defaultlocalemissing): there is no file for `defaultLocale`.
- [`localeUnreadable`](errors.md#localeunreadable): a locale file is not a JSON object. One broken file and the app reads no locale at all.

Keys used only in code (`yab.t("empty")`) are not checked: a test that runs the code in each language catches a missing one. The fake host reads the same files; `createFakeHost({ folder, context: { language: "tr" } })` answers in Turkish.


================================================================================
File: docs/testing.md
================================================================================

# Testing

An extension's tests run in Node, without the app, against a **fake host**: a stand-in for yabbistir that gives the code a `yab` (and a `fetch`) held to the app's rules. Permissions come from your manifest, calls without effects are refused the way the app refuses them, results are checked against the shapes the app accepts, and nothing reaches the network or runs a program: you give the answers.

```sh
npm test -- dev.yourname.tool                                   # one extension
npm test -- dev.yourname.tool --test-name-pattern=makesASlug     # one test
npm test                                                        # every extension
```

`npm test` runs `extensions/<id>/tests/*.test.mjs` with `node --test`. It needs **Node 22.18 or later**: tests import `src/index.ts` directly, and Node strips its types. That has two consequences for your TypeScript:

- Import types with `import type { … } from "@yabbistir/api"`. The package has no JavaScript, so a plain `import` fails at run time.
- Import your own files with their `.ts` extension: `import { parse } from "./parse.ts"`. Use only syntax Node can strip: no `enum`, no `namespace`, no constructor parameter properties.

## A test file

```js
import { describe, test } from "node:test";
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { createFakeHost, yabError } from "@yabbistir/api/fake-host";

import { actions } from "../src/index.ts";

const folder = new URL("..", import.meta.url);

describe("upper", () => {
  test("upperCasesText", async () => {
    const host = createFakeHost({ folder });
    assert.deepEqual(await host.run(actions.upper, { text: "hello" }), { text: "HELLO" });
  });
});
```

`createFakeHost({ folder })` reads `manifest.json` and `locales/*.json` from the extension's folder. Make a new host for each test when the test changes its state (files, storage, recorded calls), or share one for read-only tests.

An item needs only what matters to the test: the host fills in `id`, `tags: []` and `copiedAt`, and guesses `kind` from the fields (`url` → `link`, `files` → `file`, `image` → `image`, `color` → `color`, else `text`). Give `kind` yourself for `code`.

## Running calls

| Call | Runs | As |
|---|---|---|
| `host.run(action, item?, context?)` | `action.run(item, ctx)` | A run the person started: effects allowed, as far as the permissions go. The result is checked like the app checks it. |
| `host.hint(action, item?, context?)` | the same | A hint: no effects. |
| `host.validate(detector, item?)` | `detector.validate(item)` | Resolves to a boolean; a promise is refused. |
| `host.preview(detector, item?, context?)` | `detector.preview(item, ctx)` | No effects; the sections are checked. |
| `host.capture(rule, item?, context?)` | `rule.run(item, ctx)` | No effects; the result is checked. |

`context` sets parts of `ctx` for that call: `{ language: "tr", variant: "audio", target: { bundleID: "com.apple.finder", name: "Finder", kind: "finder" } }`. Pass `null` as the item for a generator.

A call the app would refuse rejects with the same `code`, so test the code:

```js
await assert.rejects(host.hint(actions.fetchTitle, { url: "https://example.com" }), { code: "permissionDenied" });
await assert.rejects(host.run(actions.broken, { text: "x" }), { code: "badResult" });
```

## Options

| Option | What it sets |
|---|---|
| `folder` | The extension's folder (a path or a `file:` URL): its manifest and locales. |
| `manifest` | Manifest fields over the folder's, such as `{ permissions: [] }` to test a missing permission. |
| `locales` | `{ en: { … }, tr: { … } }` instead of the folder's. |
| `item` | The item a call gets when you pass none. |
| `context` | `{ language, trigger, variant, target }` for every call. |
| `preferences` | Values the person chose in Settings; the rest come from the manifest's defaults. |
| `secrets` | `{ id: value }` for the manifest's `secret` preferences. |
| `http` | Answers for `yab.http.fetch` and `fetch` (see below). |
| `exec` | Answers for `yab.exec` (see below). |
| `ai` | An answer, or `(prompt, options) => answer`, for `yab.ai.generate`. Without it: `unavailable`. |
| `translate` | `{ text, from }`, a string, or `(text, { to, from }) => …`, for `yab.translate`. Without it: `unavailable`. |
| `vision` | `{ ocr, readCodes, removeBackground }`: answers or functions. Without one: `unavailable`. |
| `history` | The items `yab.history` returns, newest first. |
| `files` | `{ path: text or Uint8Array }`: files on the fake disk, such as an item's own files. |
| `storage` | What `yab.storage` holds at the start. |
| `now` | A `Date`, ISO text or milliseconds: `Date.now()` and `new Date()` during calls, and items' `copiedAt`. |

An answer in any table can be an `Error` to make the call fail, and `yabError(code, message)` makes one with a `code`, the way the app's errors have one.

## What the host records

| Field | Holds |
|---|---|
| `host.calls` | Every `yab` call in order, as `{ api, args }`, such as `{ api: "exec", args: ["yt-dlp", [...]] }`. Callbacks and signals are left out, and so are `t` and plain reads (`storage.get`, `files.read`, `files.exists`, `image.info`). |
| `host.results` | What each call returned. |
| `host.notifications` | The `yab.notify` messages, cut to 200 characters. |
| `host.opened` | The links `yab.open` got. |
| `host.progress` | Each `yab.job.progress` as `{ fraction, message }`. |
| `host.files` | The fake disk: a `Map` from path to bytes. |
| `host.storage` | The store. |

`host.yab` is the fake `yab` itself, and `host.cancel()` cancels the calls in progress the way the person's ✕ does.

## The network

`http` maps `"<url>"` or `"<METHOD> <url>"` (the whole URL, query included) to a response, or is a function `(request) => response` that gets `{ method, url, headers, body }`, with the headers as your code wrote them. A response is `{ status = 200, headers, text | json | body }`, an `Error`, or a function returning either.

```js
const host = createFakeHost({
  folder,
  secrets: { apiKey: "test-key" },
  http: ({ method, url, headers }) => {
    assert.equal(headers.authorization, "Bearer test-key");
    return method === "GET" && url === "https://api.example.com/v1/define?word=apple"
      ? { json: { definition: "a fruit" } }
      : { status: 404, text: "not found" };
  },
});
```

The manifest's permission and `network.domains` are checked first, as in the app: a host outside the list rejects with `permissionDenied`. A request with no answer rejects with `networkError`, so a test notices a request it did not expect.

## Jobs and programs

`exec` maps a tool's name to `{ exitCode, stdout, stderr }`, an `Error`, or `(args, { input, workDir, host }) => result`. Only tools in `requires.tools` run; one listed in the manifest but missing from the table rejects with `toolMissing`, which tests the "not installed" path. `onLine` hears the answer's lines once the tool has "finished", standard output first.

A tool that writes files writes them on the fake disk itself, in `workDir`:

```js
const host = createFakeHost({
  folder,
  exec: {
    "yt-dlp": (args, { host, workDir }) => {
      assert.equal(args.at(-2), "--", "the link comes after --");
      host.files.set(`${workDir}/video.mp4`, new Uint8Array([0]));
      host.files.set(`${workDir}/result.txt`, new TextEncoder().encode(`${workDir}/video.mp4\n`));
      return { exitCode: 0, stdout: "yab 50 100\nyab 100 100\n", stderr: "" };
    },
  },
});
const result = await host.run(actions.download, { url: "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=x" }, { variant: "video" });
assert.match(result.file, /video\.mp4$/);
```

Test cancelling by starting a call and cancelling it while it waits:

```js
const host = createFakeHost({ folder, exec: { slow: () => new Promise(() => {}) } });
const running = host.run(actions.convert, { text: "x" });
setTimeout(() => host.cancel(), 10);
await assert.rejects(running, { code: "cancelled" });
```

## Where an action is offered

The app offers an action, and runs a detector or a rule, only on items its manifest's `accepts` takes. Two helpers apply `accepts` in a test:

- `host.offers(item?, context?)` returns the ids of the actions the app would offer on the item, in the app's order: `"input": "item"` actions whose `accepts` takes it, highest `priority` first, the paste target's own actions first, and a `targetsOnly` action only for its targets (`context: { target: { … } }`).
- `acceptsMatch(accepts, item, { extensionID }?)`, exported next to `createFakeHost`, applies any one `accepts` block, such as a detector's or a rule's. `extensionID` lets a tag written as `"tag"` stand for the extension's own detector, as in the app.

```js
import fs from "node:fs";
import { acceptsMatch, createFakeHost } from "@yabbistir/api/fake-host";

const host = createFakeHost({ folder });
assert.deepEqual(host.offers({ kind: "text", text: "Ada@Example.com" }), ["lower"]);
assert.deepEqual(host.offers({ kind: "text", text: "no address here" }), []);

const manifest = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(new URL("../manifest.json", import.meta.url), "utf8"));
assert.equal(acceptsMatch(manifest.contributes.detectors[0].accepts, { kind: "text", text: "ABC-123" }), true);
```

Both check the kind (a single image file counts for `image`), the tags, and the [pattern](concepts.md#patterns), searched for in the trimmed text or URL. The app matches patterns with ICU; the helpers use JavaScript's `RegExp` with the `u` flag, after turning a leading `(?i)`, `(?s)` or `(?m)` into flags, `\d` into any decimal digit, and a bare script name such as `\p{Greek}` into `\p{Script=Greek}`. That is close to the app, not identical: `\w` and `\s` differ slightly, and ICU-only syntax (`a++`, `(?>…)`, `(?x)`, a flag group after the start, sets with `&&` or `--`, `[[:alpha:]]`, `\Q…\E`, block properties) throws an error that says so. `npm run validate` remains the judge of whether a pattern is valid ICU, and `npm run dev` shows the app's real matching.

## Everything else

- **Preferences:** `preferences: { format: "short" }`; the rest come from the manifest's defaults. A `folder` preference's `~` becomes `/Users/test`, and `yab.files.read` may read inside a folder only when the test set it in `preferences`, as when the person chose it.
- **Secrets:** `secrets: { apiKey: "test-key" }`; `yab.secrets.get` returns only declared `secret` preferences.
- **History:** `history: [ … ]`, newest first. Items come back trimmed the app's way: text and HTML cut to 64 KB with `truncated: true`, images with their size only. The `history` permission is checked.
- **AI and translation:** `ai: (prompt, options) => "A summary."`, `translate: (text, { to }) => ({ text: "Merhaba", from: "en" })`. Both refuse to run without effects.
- **Images:** handles are fake. `yab.image.convert` and `resize` work out the new size; `yab.files.write` of a handle writes placeholder bytes.
- **Time:** `now: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"` fixes the clock during calls.
- **Language:** `context: { language: "tr" }` on the host or one call; `yab.t` answers from that locale.

## What the fake host does not do

- `host.run` runs an action on whatever item you pass, whether its `accepts` takes it or not; check that with `host.offers` ([above](#where-an-action-is-offered)), and let `run` cope with an item it did not expect.
- It enforces no time limits: keep hints, validators and rules fast yourself.
- It does not limit notices to one every 3 seconds, as the app does.
- It runs no real program, request, model, translation or image operation. Test the code around them, and try the real thing with `npm run dev`.

## Testing the manifest

Some promises live in the manifest. Read it in a test when it matters:

```js
import fs from "node:fs";

test("theRuleDoesNotAskForTags", () => {
  const manifest = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(new URL("../manifest.json", import.meta.url), "utf8"));
  assert.equal(manifest.contributes.captureRules[0].accepts.tags, undefined);
});
```

Tests are Node code, so they may use `node:fs` and friends; only `src/` runs in the app.

## Libraries

Most extensions need none. When one helps, it must be plain JavaScript that runs without Node ([errors](errors.md#node-builtins)). Put it in a `package.json` in the extension's own folder, at an exact version, and run `npm install` from the repository's root:

```json
{
  "name": "dev.yourname.tool",
  "private": true,
  "type": "module",
  "dependencies": { "some-library": "1.2.3" }
}
```

The repository uses npm workspaces, so the library is installed for the whole repository and the build bundles it into `index.js`. Keep `"type": "module"`: the tests load `src/index.ts` as a module. The pull request then changes the extension's folder and the root `package-lock.json`.

## Before a pull request

`npm test -- <id>`, `npm run validate -- <id>` and `npm run build -- <id>` all pass. Cover the main path, every message the person can see (in each language you ship), and the failures you expect: no input, a missing tool, a failed request, a cancel.


================================================================================
File: docs/design-guidelines.md
================================================================================

# Design guidelines

yabbistir has one look: calm, grey, native macOS. Extensions never draw anything. They supply words, an icon and data, and the app draws the rows, tag chips, preview sections, job cards and notices in that one look. An extension's job is to make its words short and its data clean, so it reads as part of the app rather than a guest in it.

## What the app draws for you

| You give | The app draws |
|---|---|
| An action's `title`, `subtitle` and hint | A row in the panel, with your icon in the row's icon slot |
| A detector's `tag` | A small grey chip on the item |
| Preview sections | Blocks in the item's preview, in the preview's type and spacing |
| `yab.job.progress` | The job card's bar and status line |
| `{ none: true, message }`, `yab.notify`, a thrown error | A calm notice, titled with your extension's name |
| Preferences | Controls in Settings |

There is no way to pick a color, a font, a layout or a size, and that is on purpose. Do not try to get around it: no emoji as decoration, no ASCII art, no colored symbols in text, no HTML results meant as a layout. A colorful extension looks broken next to everything else, and a reviewer will ask you to remove it.

## Naming

- **The extension's name:** one to three words, in title case, saying what it is about: "Download Video", "Link Cleaner", "JWT", "Translate". No "for yabbistir", no "Pro", no version numbers.
- **Action titles:** sentence case, starting with a verb, saying what happens to the item: "Download as video", "Translate to Turkish", "Remove tracking parameters". Keep it to about 30 characters; the row has one line.
- **Variant titles:** whole titles of their own, since each is a row: "Download as video" and "Download audio", not "Video" and "Audio".
- **Subtitles:** a short fact, with " · " between parts: "MP4 · best quality", "On this Mac".
- **Tags:** one short word or an abbreviation: "JWT", "ticket". It sits in a chip beside the item.
- **Keywords:** lowercase words people would type, synonyms included: `["slug", "slugify", "url", "permalink"]`.
- **Ids** (extension, action, detector, rule) are for code, never shown: lowercase, plain, stable.

## Words

- Short and plain. Say what happened or what to do: "There is no text to translate." "This post asks you to sign in. You can turn on browser cookies for Download Video in Settings."
- No "Error:", no "Oops", no exclamation marks, no ALL CAPS. The app already marks a failure as one.
- Name the fix when there is one: "yt-dlp may need an update: brew upgrade yt-dlp".
- Notices are cut at 200 characters, and a job card's status line is cut too: put the important words first.
- Progress messages are numbers with units while a fraction is known ("18.4 / 43.7 MB · 1 min left") and a state word when it is not ("Connecting", "Merging").
- Use typographic apostrophes and quotes in strings: "Couldn’t download the video".
- Every string goes through the locale files ([Localization](localization.md)), in English at least.

## Icons

The icon appears in the row's icon slot, on job cards and in Settings, at about 13 to 16 points, in the panel's grey.

- **Use an SF Symbol** whenever one fits: `"icon": "sf:arrow.down.circle"`. The app draws it in its secondary grey, the same as its own icons, in light and dark mode. Pick an outline symbol that says the action rather than the brand. An unknown name falls back to a generic extension symbol, so check the name in the SF Symbols app.
- **A file icon** is `icon.png` next to manifest.json (the only file name the build copies), square, at least 64 × 64 pixels, drawn at 16 points. The app does not tint it, so it must read on both light and dark grey: a simple glyph in a mid grey, on a transparent background. No logos with brand colors, no gradients, no text.

## Previews

- One section per idea, with a one- or two-word title: "Header", "Payload", "Info".
- `keyValue` for short facts, `code` with a `language` for anything structured, `text` for a sentence.
- Show what the item is, not everything you can compute. Three sections is plenty.
- Say what you did not check when it matters: the JWT preview ends with "The signature isn't checked".

## Results

- Return the result in the form the person expects to paste: clean text without trailing newlines, a link as a link, a file with a good name (`Meeting notes.md`, not `output-1.txt`).
- A file's name comes from its subject when there is one, such as the video's title.
- Nothing to do is not an error: `{ none: true, message }` with one short sentence.


================================================================================
File: docs/recipes/download-with-yt-dlp.md
================================================================================

# Recipe: download video and audio with yt-dlp

A job that runs a command-line program, reports its progress, and hands back the file it made. Copy a YouTube link, open the transforms with ⇧, and pick *Download as video* or *Download audio*. With Finder in front, the file lands in the open folder.

This is a small version of [Download Video](../../extensions/dev.yabbistir.video-download), which adds Instagram and X, conversions for video and audio formats that not every Mac app plays, clearer failure messages, and optional browser cookies for posts that need a sign-in.

It shows: the `exec` permission and `requires.tools`, arguments that are safe to pass, a job with progress, variants, and a file result aimed at Finder.

```sh
npm run new -- dev.yourname.download --template job
```

Replace the template's files with these, and delete `locales/tr.json` (or translate the keys).

## manifest.json

```json file=manifest.json
{
  "id": "dev.yourname.download",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "apiVersion": 1,
  "defaultLocale": "en",
  "name": "name",
  "description": "description",
  "icon": "sf:arrow.down.circle",
  "author": "your-github-name",
  "license": "MIT",
  "categories": ["media"],
  "permissions": ["network", "exec"],
  "network": { "domains": ["youtube.com", "youtu.be"] },
  "requires": {
    "tools": [
      { "name": "yt-dlp", "install": "brew install yt-dlp" },
      { "name": "ffmpeg", "install": "brew install ffmpeg" },
      { "name": "deno", "install": "brew install deno" }
    ]
  },
  "contributes": {
    "actions": [
      { "id": "download", "title": "download.title", "keywords": "download.keywords", "input": "item",
        "accepts": { "kinds": ["link"], "pattern": "^https?://([a-z0-9-]+\\.)*(youtube\\.com|youtu\\.be)/" },
        "targets": ["finder"], "job": true, "output": "file", "verb": "verb",
        "variants": [
          { "id": "video", "title": "video.title", "subtitle": "video.subtitle", "failTitle": "video.fail" },
          { "id": "audio", "title": "audio.title", "subtitle": "audio.subtitle", "failTitle": "audio.fail" }
        ] }
    ]
  }
}
```

- `exec` runs only the tools listed. yt-dlp downloads; it calls ffmpeg to merge video and audio or to extract the audio, and deno to solve YouTube's challenges. The extension itself runs only `yt-dlp`.
- `network` with its domains is what the person reads before install: "Can reach: youtube.com, youtu.be". yt-dlp reaches the sites itself; the permission makes that plain, and holds the extension's own requests to those hosts.
- `"targets": ["finder"]` puts the action first when Finder is in front, where the file is dropped into the open folder.
- Each variant is its own row and gets its own failure title.

## locales/en.json

```json file=locales/en.json
{
  "name": "Download",
  "description": "Downloads YouTube links as MP4 video or M4A audio with yt-dlp.",
  "download.title": "Download video",
  "download.keywords": ["download", "video", "audio", "youtube", "mp4", "m4a"],
  "video.title": "Download as video",
  "video.subtitle": "MP4",
  "video.fail": "Couldn’t download the video",
  "audio.title": "Download audio",
  "audio.subtitle": "M4A · audio only",
  "audio.fail": "Couldn’t download the audio",
  "verb": "Download",
  "connecting": "Connecting",
  "progress": "{done} / {total} MB",
  "update": "Couldn’t download. yt-dlp may need an update: brew upgrade yt-dlp",
  "noFile": "The downloaded file could not be found."
}
```

## src/index.ts

```ts file=src/index.ts
import type { Actions } from "@yabbistir/api";

/** One line per update, "yab <bytes done> <bytes in all>", with "NA" for a number yt-dlp does not know yet. */
const progressTemplate = "download:yab %(progress.downloaded_bytes)s %(progress.total_bytes)s";

/**
 * yt-dlp's arguments: fixed flags, then the link after "--", so a link that looks like an option
 * ("--exec=…") is still only a link. No shell reads them.
 */
export function ytDlpArguments(url: string, variant: string, workDir: string): string[] {
  const kind = variant === "audio"
    ? ["-f", "ba/b", "-x", "--audio-format", "m4a"]
    : ["-S", "vcodec:h264,res,acodec:aac", "--merge-output-format", "mp4"];
  return [
    "--newline", "--no-playlist", "--no-mtime",
    "--progress-template", progressTemplate,
    "-o", `${workDir}/%(title).120B.%(ext)s`,
    // Writes the finished file's path to a file. Unlike --print, it keeps the progress lines coming.
    "--print-to-file", "after_move:filepath", `${workDir}/result.txt`,
    ...kind,
    "--", url,
  ];
}

/** Bytes done and in all from a progress line; undefined for any other line, or while the size is unknown. */
export function progressOf(line: string): { done: number; total: number } | undefined {
  const [tag, done, total] = line.trim().split(/\s+/);
  if (tag !== "yab" || !(Number(done) >= 0) || !(Number(total) > 0)) return undefined;
  return { done: Number(done), total: Number(total) };
}

const megabytes = (bytes: number) => (bytes / 1e6).toFixed(1);

export const actions: Actions = {
  download: {
    async run(item, ctx) {
      const url = item?.url ?? item?.text ?? "";
      const workDir = yab.files.workDir;
      yab.job.progress(null, yab.t("connecting"));
      let lastPercent = -1;
      // A missing tool, a cancel or a refused permission rejects from here with its own code: let it through.
      const result = await yab.exec("yt-dlp", ytDlpArguments(url, ctx.variant ?? "video", workDir), {
        signal: ctx.signal,
        onLine(line, stream) {
          const progress = stream === "stdout" ? progressOf(line) : undefined;
          if (!progress) return;
          const percent = Math.floor((progress.done / progress.total) * 100);
          if (percent === lastPercent) return; // once per whole percent, so the card redraws calmly
          lastPercent = percent;
          yab.job.progress(progress.done / progress.total,
            yab.t("progress", { done: megabytes(progress.done), total: megabytes(progress.total) }));
        },
```
