```ts file=src/index.ts
      });
      if (result.exitCode !== 0) throw new Error(yab.t("update"));

      const printed = `${workDir}/result.txt`;
      const path = yab.files.exists(printed) ? new TextDecoder().decode(yab.files.read(printed)).trim().split("\n").pop() ?? "" : "";
      if (path === "" || !yab.files.exists(path)) throw new Error(yab.t("noFile"));
      return { file: path };
    },
  },
};
```

- **Arguments are fixed, and the link comes last, after `--`.** The review checks this for every extension with `exec` ([checklist](../review-checklist.md#exec)). Never add options that run other programs, such as `--exec`.
- yt-dlp writes into the call's work folder, so the file is a valid result; the app moves it into its own output folder afterwards.
- A non-zero exit code is not an error by itself: the code checks it and fails with a message the person can act on.

## tests/index.test.mjs

The fake host never runs yt-dlp: the test gives a stand-in that prints progress lines and leaves a file on the fake disk, as the real one would.

```js file=tests/index.test.mjs
import { describe, test } from "node:test";
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { createFakeHost } from "@yabbistir/api/fake-host";

import { actions, ytDlpArguments } from "../src/index.ts";

const folder = new URL("..", import.meta.url);
const link = { kind: "link", url: "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=abc" };

/** Prints two progress lines and leaves the file where -o says, with its path in result.txt. */
function fakeYtDlp(seen = []) {
  return (args, { host, workDir }) => {
    seen.push(args);
    const file = `${workDir}/Clip.${args.includes("-x") ? "m4a" : "mp4"}`;
    host.files.set(file, new Uint8Array([0]));
    host.files.set(`${workDir}/result.txt`, new TextEncoder().encode(`${file}\n`));
    return { exitCode: 0, stdout: "yab 1000000 4000000\nyab 4000000 4000000\n", stderr: "" };
  };
}

describe("download", () => {
  test("theLinkComesLastAfterTheOptionTerminator", () => {
    const args = ytDlpArguments("--exec=touch /tmp/x", "video", "/work");
    assert.deepEqual(args.slice(-2), ["--", "--exec=touch /tmp/x"]);
    assert.ok(!args.includes("--exec"));
  });

  test("downloadsAVideoAndReportsProgress", async () => {
    const seen = [];
    const host = createFakeHost({ folder, exec: { "yt-dlp": fakeYtDlp(seen) } });
    const result = await host.run(actions.download, link, { variant: "video" });
    assert.match(result.file, /Clip\.mp4$/);
    assert.ok(seen[0].includes("--merge-output-format"));
    assert.deepEqual(host.progress.map((entry) => entry.fraction), [null, 0.25, 1]);
    assert.equal(host.progress[1].message, "1.0 / 4.0 MB");
  });

  test("audioAsksForM4a", async () => {
    const seen = [];
    const host = createFakeHost({ folder, exec: { "yt-dlp": fakeYtDlp(seen) } });
    const result = await host.run(actions.download, link, { variant: "audio" });
    assert.match(result.file, /Clip\.m4a$/);
    assert.ok(seen[0].includes("-x"));
  });

  test("aFailedRunSaysToUpdate", async () => {
    const host = createFakeHost({ folder, exec: { "yt-dlp": () => ({ exitCode: 1, stdout: "", stderr: "ERROR: Unsupported URL" }) } });
    await assert.rejects(host.run(actions.download, link, { variant: "video" }), /brew upgrade yt-dlp/);
  });

  test("aMissingToolSaysHowToInstallIt", async () => {
    const host = createFakeHost({ folder });
    await assert.rejects(host.run(actions.download, link, { variant: "video" }), { code: "toolMissing", message: /brew install yt-dlp/ });
  });
});
```


# Recipe: call an API with a key

An action that sends the selected word to a web service and pastes the answer, with the person's API key kept in the Keychain. The service here, `api.example.com`, stands in for yours: it answers `GET /v1/define?word=<word>` with `{ "word": …, "definition": … }`, and wants the key as a bearer token.

It shows: the `network` permission held to one host, a `secret` preference, `yab.http.fetch`, and turning a service's answers into results and messages.

```sh
npm run new -- dev.yourname.define --template action
```

Replace the template's files with these, and delete `locales/tr.json` (or translate the keys).

## manifest.json

```json file=manifest.json
{
  "id": "dev.yourname.define",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "apiVersion": 1,
  "defaultLocale": "en",
  "name": "name",
  "description": "description",
  "icon": "sf:character.book.closed",
  "author": "your-github-name",
  "license": "MIT",
  "categories": ["text"],
  "permissions": ["network"],
  "network": { "domains": ["api.example.com"] },
  "preferences": [
    { "id": "apiKey", "type": "secret", "title": "apiKey.title" }
  ],
  "contributes": {
    "actions": [
      { "id": "define", "title": "define.title", "keywords": "define.keywords", "input": "item",
        "accepts": { "kinds": ["text"], "pattern": "^[\\p{L}'-]{2,40}$" }, "output": "text" }
    ]
  }
}
```

- `network.domains` names the one host. The person reads "Can reach: api.example.com", and any other host is refused.
- The `secret` preference appears in Settings as a field the person pastes the key into. It is kept in the Keychain, never in `yab.preferences`, and has no default.
- The pattern offers the action only on a single word.
- No `hint`: hints run without effects, and a request is an effect. The action runs when the person picks it.

## locales/en.json

```json file=locales/en.json
{
  "name": "Define",
  "description": "Looks up the copied word in a dictionary service.",
  "apiKey.title": "API key",
  "define.title": "Define word",
  "define.keywords": ["define", "definition", "dictionary", "meaning"],
  "noKey": "Add your API key in Settings → Extensions → Define.",
  "badKey": "The service did not accept the API key. Check it in Settings.",
  "notFound": "No definition found for “{word}”.",
  "serviceFailed": "The dictionary service did not answer (status {status}). Try again later."
}
```

## src/index.ts

```ts file=src/index.ts
import type { Actions } from "@yabbistir/api";

const endpoint = "https://api.example.com/v1/define";

export const actions: Actions = {
  define: {
    async run(item, ctx) {
      const word = (item?.text ?? "").trim();
      const key = yab.secrets.get("apiKey");
      if (key === null || key === "") return { none: true, message: yab.t("noKey") };

      // No connection rejects with "networkError", which the app reports itself: let it through.
      const response = await yab.http.fetch(`${endpoint}?word=${encodeURIComponent(word)}`, {
        headers: { authorization: `Bearer ${key}`, accept: "application/json" },
        signal: ctx.signal,
      });
      if (response.status === 401 || response.status === 403) return { none: true, message: yab.t("badKey") };
      if (response.status === 404) return { none: true, message: yab.t("notFound", { word }) };

      let definition: unknown;
      try {
        definition = (JSON.parse(response.text ?? "") as { definition?: unknown }).definition;
      } catch {
        definition = undefined;
      }
      if (response.status !== 200 || typeof definition !== "string") {
        return { none: true, message: yab.t("serviceFailed", { status: response.status }) };
      }
      return { text: definition.trim() };
    },
  },
};
```

- The key is read with `yab.secrets.get` when needed, sent only to its own service, and never logged or returned.
- A service that is down is not the extension's failure, so the code answers with a message (`{ none: true, message }`) instead of throwing. In an action, thrown errors count toward turning the extension off ([errors](../errors.md#turned-off-after-repeated-errors)).
- `yab.http.fetch` gives the body as `text` and lowercases header names. The web `fetch` works too, held to the same rules.

## tests/index.test.mjs

```js file=tests/index.test.mjs
import { describe, test } from "node:test";
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { createFakeHost, yabError } from "@yabbistir/api/fake-host";

import { actions } from "../src/index.ts";

const folder = new URL("..", import.meta.url);
const word = (text) => ({ kind: "text", text });

/** The service: one known word, and the key checked. */
function service({ url, headers }) {
  if (headers.authorization !== "Bearer test-key") return { status: 401, text: "" };
  if (url === "https://api.example.com/v1/define?word=serendipity") {
    return { json: { word: "serendipity", definition: "Finding something good without looking for it." } };
  }
  return { status: 404, text: "" };
}

describe("define", () => {
  test("looksUpTheWordWithTheKey", async () => {
    const host = createFakeHost({ folder, secrets: { apiKey: "test-key" }, http: service });
    assert.deepEqual(await host.run(actions.define, word("serendipity")), { text: "Finding something good without looking for it." });
  });

  test("saysWhenTheWordIsUnknown", async () => {
    const host = createFakeHost({ folder, secrets: { apiKey: "test-key" }, http: service });
    assert.deepEqual(await host.run(actions.define, word("zzzz")), { none: true, message: "No definition found for “zzzz”." });
  });

  test("asksForTheKeyBeforeAnyRequest", async () => {
    const host = createFakeHost({ folder, http: service });
    const result = await host.run(actions.define, word("serendipity"));
    assert.equal(result.message, "Add your API key in Settings → Extensions → Define.");
    assert.ok(!host.calls.some((call) => call.api === "http.fetch"));
  });

  test("explainsARejectedKey", async () => {
    const host = createFakeHost({ folder, secrets: { apiKey: "wrong" }, http: service });
    assert.equal((await host.run(actions.define, word("serendipity"))).message, "The service did not accept the API key. Check it in Settings.");
  });

  test("aServerErrorIsAMessageNotAFailure", async () => {
    const host = createFakeHost({ folder, secrets: { apiKey: "test-key" }, http: () => ({ status: 503, text: "busy" }) });
    assert.deepEqual(await host.run(actions.define, word("serendipity")),
      { none: true, message: "The dictionary service did not answer (status 503). Try again later." });
  });

  test("noConnectionIsLetThrough", async () => {
    const host = createFakeHost({ folder, secrets: { apiKey: "test-key" }, http: () => yabError("networkError", "offline") });
    await assert.rejects(host.run(actions.define, word("serendipity")), { code: "networkError" });
  });

  test("neverRunsAsAHint", async () => {
    const host = createFakeHost({ folder, secrets: { apiKey: "test-key" }, http: service });
    await assert.rejects(host.hint(actions.define, word("serendipity")), { code: "permissionDenied" });
  });
});
```

## Try it

```sh
npm test -- dev.yourname.define
npm run validate -- dev.yourname.define
npm run dev -- dev.yourname.define
```

Point `endpoint` and `network.domains` at your real service first. In yabbistir, approve the permission and paste your key in Settings → Extensions → Define. The README must say what is sent where: the selected word, to your service, when the person runs the action.

# Recipe: tag and preview

A detector that recognizes copied UUIDs, tags them, and shows their version and, for time-based ones, when they were made. An action, offered only on tagged items, pastes the UUID without its dashes.

It shows: a detector with `validate` and `preview`, the item's tags, and an action with `accepts.tags`. [JWT](../../extensions/dev.yabbistir.jwt) is a real detector built the same way.

```sh
npm run new -- dev.yourname.uuid-info --template detector
```

Replace the template's files with these, and delete `locales/tr.json` (or translate the keys).

## manifest.json

```json file=manifest.json
{
  "id": "dev.yourname.uuid-info",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "apiVersion": 1,
  "defaultLocale": "en",
  "name": "name",
  "description": "description",
  "icon": "sf:number",
  "author": "your-github-name",
  "license": "MIT",
  "categories": ["developer"],
  "contributes": {
    "detectors": [
      { "id": "uuid", "tag": "tag",
        "accepts": { "kinds": ["text", "code"], "pattern": "^[0-9A-Fa-f]{8}-[0-9A-Fa-f]{4}-[0-9A-Fa-f]{4}-[0-9A-Fa-f]{4}-[0-9A-Fa-f]{12}$" },
        "validate": true, "preview": true }
    ],
    "actions": [
      { "id": "compact", "title": "compact.title", "keywords": "compact.keywords", "input": "item",
        "accepts": { "kinds": ["text", "code"], "tags": ["uuid"] }, "output": "text", "hint": true }
    ]
  }
}
```

- The detector's `pattern` does the cheap work without any code: only text shaped like a UUID is a candidate. `validate` then has the last word.
- `"tags": ["uuid"]` on the action names the extension's own detector by its id; the item carries it as `dev.yourname.uuid-info:uuid`. Another extension's tag is written in full.
- The detector needs no permission: it reads only the item.

## locales/en.json

```json file=locales/en.json
{
  "name": "UUID Info",
  "description": "Recognizes copied UUIDs and shows their version and time.",
  "tag": "UUID",
  "preview": "UUID",
  "version": "Version",
  "created": "Created",
  "compact.title": "Remove dashes",
  "compact.keywords": ["uuid", "dashes", "compact", "hex"],
  "notAUUID": "This is not a UUID."
}
```

## src/index.ts

```ts file=src/index.ts
import type { Actions, Detectors, Item, PreviewSection } from "@yabbistir/api";

const shape = /^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$/i;
/** 100-nanosecond steps between 1582-10-15 (where version 1 counts from) and 1970-01-01. */
const gregorianOffset = 122_192_928_000_000_000n;

/** The item's UUID in lowercase, or null when the item is not one. */
export function uuidOf(item: Item): string | null {
  const text = (item.text ?? "").trim();
  return shape.test(text) ? text.toLowerCase() : null;
}

/** The version (1–8, 0 for the nil UUID, 15 for the max UUID) and, for versions 1 and 7, when it was made. */
export function inspect(uuid: string): { version: number; created?: Date } {
  const hex = uuid.replace(/-/g, "");
  const version = parseInt(hex[12], 16);
  if (version === 7) return { version, created: new Date(parseInt(hex.slice(0, 12), 16)) };
  if (version === 1) {
    const ticks = BigInt(`0x${hex.slice(13, 16)}${hex.slice(8, 12)}${hex.slice(0, 8)}`);
    return { version, created: new Date(Number((ticks - gregorianOffset) / 10_000n)) };
  }
  return { version };
}

export const detectors: Detectors = {
  uuid: {
    // Quick and without promises. Anything unexpected is false, never a throw.
    validate(item) {
      const uuid = uuidOf(item);
      if (uuid === null) return false;
      const { version } = inspect(uuid);
      return (version >= 1 && version <= 8) || /^0+$|^f+$/.test(uuid.replace(/-/g, ""));
    },
    // Runs when the preview opens, without effects. The app draws the sections.
    preview(item): PreviewSection[] {
      const uuid = uuidOf(item);
      if (uuid === null) return [];
      const { version, created } = inspect(uuid);
      const rows: [string, string][] = [[yab.t("version"), String(version)]];
      if (created !== undefined && !Number.isNaN(created.getTime())) rows.push([yab.t("created"), created.toISOString()]);
      return [{ type: "keyValue", title: yab.t("preview"), rows }];
    },
  },
};

export const actions: Actions = {
  compact: {
    run(item) {
      const uuid = item === null ? null : uuidOf(item);
      if (uuid === null) return { none: true, message: yab.t("notAUUID") };
      return { text: uuid.replace(/-/g, "") };
    },
  },
};
```

## tests/index.test.mjs

```js file=tests/index.test.mjs
import { describe, test } from "node:test";
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import fs from "node:fs";
import { createFakeHost } from "@yabbistir/api/fake-host";

import { actions, detectors } from "../src/index.ts";

const host = createFakeHost({ folder: new URL("..", import.meta.url) });
const text = (value) => ({ kind: "text", text: value });
const V7 = "019b76da-a800-7abc-9def-0123456789ab"; // made at 2026-01-01 00:00 UTC
const V1 = "d0c3c000-e6a4-11f0-8000-0a1b2c3d4e5f"; // the same moment
const V4 = "3f2b8c1e-9a4d-4f6e-8b2a-1c3d5e7f9a0b";

describe("uuid", () => {
  test("tagsUUIDs", async () => {
    for (const uuid of [V7, V1, V4, V4.toUpperCase(), "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"]) {
      assert.equal(await host.validate(detectors.uuid, text(uuid)), true, uuid);
    }
  });

  test("leavesOtherTextAlone", async () => {
    assert.equal(await host.validate(detectors.uuid, text("not a uuid")), false);
    assert.equal(await host.validate(detectors.uuid, text("3f2b8c1e-9a4d-9f6e-8b2a-1c3d5e7f9a0b")), false, "version 9 does not exist");
  });

  test("previewShowsTheVersionAndTime", async () => {
    assert.deepEqual(await host.preview(detectors.uuid, text(V7)),
      [{ type: "keyValue", title: "UUID", rows: [["Version", "7"], ["Created", "2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z"]] }]);
    const [section] = await host.preview(detectors.uuid, text(V1));
    assert.deepEqual(section.rows[1], ["Created", "2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z"]);
  });

  test("previewOfARandomUUIDHasNoTime", async () => {
    const [section] = await host.preview(detectors.uuid, text(V4));
    assert.deepEqual(section.rows, [["Version", "4"]]);
  });

  test("compactRemovesTheDashes", async () => {
    assert.deepEqual(await host.hint(actions.compact, text(V4)), { text: "3f2b8c1e9a4d4f6e8b2a1c3d5e7f9a0b" });
  });

  test("theActionIsOfferedOnlyOnTaggedItems", () => {
    const manifest = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(new URL("../manifest.json", import.meta.url), "utf8"));
    assert.deepEqual(manifest.contributes.actions[0].accepts.tags, ["uuid"]);
  });
});
```

## Try it

```sh
npm test -- dev.yourname.uuid-info
npm run validate -- dev.yourname.uuid-info
npm run dev -- dev.yourname.uuid-info
```

Copy a UUID: its item gets the *UUID* chip, its preview shows the version, and ⇧ on it offers *Remove dashes*. UUIDs already in your history are tagged too, in the background, once the extension loads.

# Recipe: a link-cleaning rule

A capture rule that removes tracking parameters from links as they are copied, so `https://example.com/p?id=7&utm_source=mail` is stored as `https://example.com/p?id=7`, and the next ⌘V pastes the clean link.

It shows: the `capture` permission, a rule's `accepts`, the `replace` and `keep` results, and keeping a rule pure and fast. [Link Cleaner](../../extensions/dev.yabbistir.link-clean) is the real extension, with a longer list of parameters and hosts.

```sh
npm run new -- dev.yourname.clean-links --template capture-rule
```

Replace the template's files with these, and delete `locales/tr.json` (or translate the keys).

## manifest.json

```json file=manifest.json
{
  "id": "dev.yourname.clean-links",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "apiVersion": 1,
  "defaultLocale": "en",
  "name": "name",
  "description": "description",
  "icon": "sf:link",
  "author": "your-github-name",
  "license": "MIT",
  "categories": ["links"],
  "permissions": ["capture"],
  "contributes": {
    "captureRules": [
      { "id": "clean", "title": "clean.title", "description": "clean.description",
        "accepts": { "kinds": ["link", "text"], "pattern": "(?i)^\\s*https?://\\S+\\s*$" } }
    ]
  }
}
```

- `capture` is what the person reads as "Can see everything you copy". It is needed for any rule, and for nothing else.
- `accepts` lets only a copied link, or text that is one address and nothing else, reach the code. `(?i)` is ICU for "ignore case".
- No `tags`: rules run before detectors tag anything, so a rule never sees tags ([`captureRuleTags`](../errors.md#captureruletags)).
- `title` and `description` show in Settings, where the person can turn the rule off.

## locales/en.json

```json file=locales/en.json
{
  "name": "Clean Links",
  "description": "Removes tracking parameters from the links you copy.",
  "clean.title": "Remove tracking parameters",
  "clean.description": "Drops utm_* and click ids from copied links."
}
```

## src/index.ts

```ts file=src/index.ts
import type { CaptureResult, CaptureRules } from "@yabbistir/api";

/** Dropped on every host. */
const everywhere = /^(utm_[a-z_]+|fbclid|gclid|dclid|msclkid|mc_cid|mc_eid)$/i;
/** Dropped only on these hosts and their subdomains. */
const perHost: [string, RegExp][] = [
  ["youtube.com", /^(si|feature|pp)$/],
  ["youtu.be", /^(si|feature)$/],
];

const parts = /^(https?:\/\/)([^/?#]*)([^?#]*)(?:\?([^#]*))?(#[\s\S]*)?$/i;

function decoded(name: string): string {
  try {
    return decodeURIComponent(name);
  } catch {
    return name;
  }
}

/**
 * The link without tracking parameters, or null when there are none. The rest of the link is kept
 * character for character: rebuilding it with `URL` would change how it is written.
 */
export function clean(link: string): string | null {
  const match = parts.exec(link.trim());
  if (!match || match[4] === undefined) return null;
  const [, scheme, authority, path, query, fragment = ""] = match;
  const host = authority.replace(/^.*@/, "").replace(/:\d*$/, "").toLowerCase();
  const local = perHost.find(([domain]) => host === domain || host.endsWith(`.${domain}`))?.[1];
  const pairs = query.split("&");
  const kept = pairs.filter((pair) => {
    const name = decoded(pair.split("=")[0]);
    return pair === "" || !(everywhere.test(name) || local?.test(name));
  });
  if (kept.length === pairs.length) return null;
  return `${scheme}${authority}${path}${kept.length > 0 ? `?${kept.join("&")}` : ""}${fragment}`;
}

export const captureRules: CaptureRules = {
  clean: {
    // Pure and fast: no yab calls, nothing awaited. Keep the copy whenever unsure.
    run(item): CaptureResult {
      if (item.kind === "link" && item.url) {
        const cleaned = clean(item.url);
        return cleaned === null ? { keep: true } : { replace: { url: cleaned } };
      }
      const cleaned = clean(item.text ?? "");
      return cleaned === null ? { keep: true } : { replace: { text: cleaned } };
    },
  },
};
```

- `{ replace: { url } }` stores a link, `{ replace: { text } }` plain text; the kind stays what it was. The app also writes the clean form to the clipboard if the clipboard still holds that copy.
- Everything the rule needs is in the item. A rule has 200 ms, no network and no other `yab` effects; past its time or on an error it is skipped and the copy is stored as it is.

## tests/index.test.mjs

```js file=tests/index.test.mjs
import { describe, test } from "node:test";
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import fs from "node:fs";
import { createFakeHost } from "@yabbistir/api/fake-host";

import { captureRules, clean } from "../src/index.ts";

const host = createFakeHost({ folder: new URL("..", import.meta.url) });
const link = (url) => ({ kind: "link", url });

describe("clean", () => {
  test("dropsTrackingParameters", async () => {
    assert.deepEqual(await host.capture(captureRules.clean, link("https://example.com/p?id=7&utm_source=mail&fbclid=1")),
      { replace: { url: "https://example.com/p?id=7" } });
  });

  test("dropsTheQuestionMarkWhenNothingIsLeft", () => {
    assert.equal(clean("https://example.com/p?utm_medium=x#top"), "https://example.com/p#top");
  });

  test("cleansTextThatIsOneAddress", async () => {
    assert.deepEqual(await host.capture(captureRules.clean, { kind: "text", text: " https://example.com/?gclid=9 " }),
      { replace: { text: "https://example.com/" } });
  });

  test("hostRulesApplyOnlyToTheirHosts", () => {
    assert.equal(clean("https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=x&si=abc"), "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=x");
    assert.equal(clean("https://example.com/?si=abc"), null);
  });

  test("keepsACleanLink", async () => {
    assert.deepEqual(await host.capture(captureRules.clean, link("https://example.com/p?id=7")), { keep: true });
  });

  test("theRuleDoesNotAskForTags", () => {
    const manifest = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(new URL("../manifest.json", import.meta.url), "utf8"));
    assert.equal(manifest.contributes.captureRules[0].accepts.tags, undefined);
  });
});
```

## Try it

```sh

npm run validate -- dev.yourname.clean-links
npm run dev -- dev.yourname.clean-links
```

In yabbistir, approve the `capture` permission in Settings → Extensions, then copy a link with `?utm_source=…`: history shows it without, and ⌘V pastes it clean.

# Recipe: translate and summarize on the Mac

Two actions on copied text: *Translate to English* and *Translate to Turkish* with the system's translation, and *Summarize* with Apple Intelligence, the on-device model. Nothing leaves the Mac, so neither needs a permission.

It shows: `yab.translate`, `yab.ai.generate`, variants, a job for the slower call, and letting the app's own messages through. [Translate](../../extensions/dev.yabbistir.translate) is the real extension.

```sh
npm run new -- dev.yourname.translate --template action
```

Replace the template's files with these, and delete `locales/tr.json` (or translate the keys).

## manifest.json

```json file=manifest.json
{
  "id": "dev.yourname.translate",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "apiVersion": 1,
  "defaultLocale": "en",
  "name": "name",
  "description": "description",
  "icon": "sf:character.bubble",
  "author": "your-github-name",
  "license": "MIT",
  "categories": ["text", "ai"],
  "contributes": {
    "actions": [
      { "id": "translate", "title": "translate.title", "keywords": "translate.keywords", "input": "item",
        "accepts": { "kinds": ["text"] }, "output": "text",
        "variants": [
          { "id": "en", "title": "en.title", "subtitle": "onThisMac" },
          { "id": "tr", "title": "tr.title", "subtitle": "onThisMac" }
        ] },
      { "id": "summarize", "title": "summarize.title", "keywords": "summarize.keywords", "input": "item",
        "accepts": { "kinds": ["text"] }, "output": "text", "job": true, "verb": "summarize.verb", "failTitle": "summarize.failed" }
    ]
  }
}
```

- The two variants are two rows; `ctx.variant` is `"en"` or `"tr"`.
- Summarizing can take several seconds, so it is a job: the card shows it working, and the person can cancel. Translation is quick enough for an action.
- No permissions: translation and the on-device model are the app's services.

## locales/en.json

```json file=locales/en.json
{
  "name": "Translate",
  "description": "Translates and summarizes text on this Mac.",
  "translate.title": "Translate",
  "translate.keywords": ["translate", "translation", "english", "turkish"],
  "en.title": "Translate to English",
  "tr.title": "Translate to Turkish",
  "onThisMac": "On this Mac",
  "already.en": "The text is already in English.",
  "already.tr": "The text is already in Turkish.",
  "empty": "There is no text to work on.",
  "summarize.title": "Summarize",
  "summarize.keywords": ["summarize", "summary", "shorten", "tl;dr"],
  "summarize.verb": "Summarize",
  "summarize.failed": "Couldn’t summarize",
  "summarizing": "Summarizing",
  "instructions": "Summarize the text in at most three sentences, in the language it is written in. Write only the summary."
}
```

## src/index.ts

```ts file=src/index.ts
import type { Actions } from "@yabbistir/api";

/** The model reads a few thousand words at most; longer text is cut first, never in the middle of a character. */
export const maxCharacters = 6000;

export function cut(text: string, limit = maxCharacters): string {
  const characters = Array.from(new Intl.Segmenter(undefined, { granularity: "grapheme" }).segment(text), (part) => part.segment);
  return characters.length <= limit ? text : characters.slice(0, limit).join("");
}

// The app's errors (no language pack, Apple Intelligence turned off, a cancel) are never caught here:
// they carry the app's own message, in the person's language.
export const actions: Actions = {
  translate: {
    async run(item, ctx) {
      const text = item?.text ?? "";
      if (text.trim() === "") return { none: true, message: yab.t("empty") };
      const to = ctx.variant === "tr" ? "tr" : "en";
      const result = await yab.translate(text, { to });
      // A text already in the target language comes back as it is; say so instead of pasting a copy.
      if (result.from.split("-")[0].toLowerCase() === to) return { none: true, message: yab.t(`already.${to}`) };
      return { text: result.text };
    },
  },
  summarize: {
    async run(item) {
      const text = (item?.text ?? "").trim();
      if (text === "") return { none: true, message: yab.t("empty") };
      yab.job.progress(null, yab.t("summarizing"));
      const summary = await yab.ai.generate(cut(text), { instructions: yab.t("instructions"), temperature: 0.3, maxTokens: 300 });
      return { text: summary.trim() };
    },
  },
};
```

- `yab.translate` recognizes the source language when `from` is left out, and says which it was.
- `yab.ai.generate` rejects with `unavailable` when this Mac cannot run the model, it is turned off, or still getting ready; the message says which. Let it through.
- Both work only in a run the person started: never as a hint, in a detector or in a rule.

## tests/index.test.mjs

```js file=tests/index.test.mjs
import { describe, test } from "node:test";
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { createFakeHost, yabError } from "@yabbistir/api/fake-host";

import { actions, cut } from "../src/index.ts";

const folder = new URL("..", import.meta.url);
const text = (value) => ({ kind: "text", text: value });

describe("translate", () => {
  test("translatesToTheChosenLanguage", async () => {
    const seen = [];
    const host = createFakeHost({ folder, translate: (input, options) => {
      seen.push(options);
      return { text: "Merhaba dünya", from: "en" };
    } });
    assert.deepEqual(await host.run(actions.translate, text("Hello world"), { variant: "tr" }), { text: "Merhaba dünya" });
    assert.deepEqual(seen, [{ to: "tr" }]);
  });

  test("saysSoWhenTheTextIsAlreadyInThatLanguage", async () => {
    const host = createFakeHost({ folder, translate: (input) => ({ text: input, from: "en-GB" }) });
    assert.deepEqual(await host.run(actions.translate, text("Hello"), { variant: "en" }), { none: true, message: "The text is already in English." });
  });

  test("letsTheAppsMessageThrough", async () => {
    const host = createFakeHost({ folder, translate: () => yabError("unavailable", "The language pack isn’t downloaded.") });
    await assert.rejects(host.run(actions.translate, text("Hello"), { variant: "tr" }), { code: "unavailable", message: "The language pack isn’t downloaded." });
  });
});

describe("summarize", () => {
  test("summarizesWithTheInstructions", async () => {
    const seen = [];
    const host = createFakeHost({ folder, ai: (prompt, options) => {
      seen.push({ prompt, options });
      return " A short summary. ";
    } });
    assert.deepEqual(await host.run(actions.summarize, text("A long text.")), { text: "A short summary." });
    assert.equal(seen[0].prompt, "A long text.");
    assert.match(seen[0].options.instructions, /three sentences/);
    assert.deepEqual(host.progress, [{ fraction: null, message: "Summarizing" }]);
  });

  test("cutsLongTextOnACharacterBoundary", () => {
    assert.equal(cut("ab👍🏽cd", 3), "ab👍🏽");
  });

  test("anUnavailableModelIsLetThrough", async () => {
    const host = createFakeHost({ folder });
    await assert.rejects(host.run(actions.summarize, text("Text")), { code: "unavailable" });
  });

  test("neverRunsWithoutThePersonAsking", async () => {
    const host = createFakeHost({ folder, ai: "unused" });
    await assert.rejects(host.hint(actions.summarize, text("Text")), { code: "permissionDenied" });
  });
});
```

## Try it

```sh
npm test -- dev.yourname.translate
npm run validate -- dev.yourname.translate
npm run dev -- dev.yourname.translate
```

Summarizing needs Apple Intelligence turned on in System Settings. A missing translation language pack is offered for download by the app itself.

# Recipe: drop a file into Finder

An action that saves copied text as a Markdown note, named after its first line. With Finder in front, pasting it drops `Meeting notes.md` into the open folder.

It shows: writing a file with `yab.files.write`, a `file` result, and `targets` with `targetsOnly`. yabbistir's built-in *Paste to Finder as a File* does this for any item; this recipe shows how an extension makes its own file. [Download Video](../../extensions/dev.yabbistir.video-download) returns a file the same way, made by a program.

```sh
npm run new -- dev.yourname.save-note --template action
```

Replace the template's files with these, and delete `locales/tr.json` (or translate the keys).

## manifest.json

```json file=manifest.json
{
  "id": "dev.yourname.save-note",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "apiVersion": 1,
  "defaultLocale": "en",
  "name": "name",
  "description": "description",
  "icon": "sf:doc.text",
  "author": "your-github-name",
  "license": "MIT",
  "categories": ["files", "text"],
  "contributes": {
    "actions": [
      { "id": "saveNote", "title": "saveNote.title", "subtitle": "saveNote.subtitle", "keywords": "saveNote.keywords",
        "input": "item", "accepts": { "kinds": ["text", "code"] }, "output": "file",
        "targets": ["finder"], "targetsOnly": true }
    ]
  }
}
```

- `"output": "file"`: `run` returns `{ file }`, a path in the call's work folder.
- `"targets": ["finder"]` with `"targetsOnly": true`: the action is offered only while Finder is the paste target, and comes first there. Anywhere else it would only paste a file reference, which is not what the person wants.
- No permission: writing in the work folder needs none, and the app moves the file to Finder.

## locales/en.json

```json file=locales/en.json
{
  "name": "Save Note",
  "description": "Saves copied text as a Markdown note in Finder.",
  "saveNote.title": "Save as Markdown note",
  "saveNote.subtitle": "Named after its first line",
  "saveNote.keywords": ["save", "note", "markdown", "file", "md"],
  "untitled": "Untitled note",
  "empty": "There is no text to save."
}
```

## src/index.ts

```ts file=src/index.ts
import type { Actions } from "@yabbistir/api";

/** "# Meeting notes" → "Meeting notes.md": the first line that has text, without Markdown heading marks or path characters. */
export function noteName(text: string, fallback: string): string {
  const first = text.split(/\r?\n/).find((line) => line.trim() !== "") ?? "";
  const clean = first.replace(/^\s*#+\s*/, "").replace(/[/:\\]/g, "-").replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim();
  const short = Array.from(clean).slice(0, 60).join("").trim();
  return `${short || fallback}.md`;
}

export const actions: Actions = {
  saveNote: {
    run(item) {
      const text = item?.text ?? "";
      if (text.trim() === "") return { none: true, message: yab.t("empty") };
      // The work folder is the only place an extension writes; a file result must be there.
      const file = yab.files.write(noteName(text, yab.t("untitled")), text.endsWith("\n") ? text : `${text}\n`);
      return { file };
    },
  },
};
```

- `yab.files.write(name, data)` returns the file's path. `/` and `:` in a name become `-`, and `..` or an empty name is refused, but a good name is the extension's job.
- The work folder is removed when the call ends, unless the result names its files; then the app takes them into its output folder, Finder gets its copy, and the file joins history.

## tests/index.test.mjs

```js file=tests/index.test.mjs
import { describe, test } from "node:test";
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import fs from "node:fs";
import { createFakeHost } from "@yabbistir/api/fake-host";

import { actions, noteName } from "../src/index.ts";

const folder = new URL("..", import.meta.url);
const finder = { target: { bundleID: "com.apple.finder", name: "Finder", kind: "finder" } };

describe("saveNote", () => {
  test("savesTheTextAsAMarkdownFile", async () => {
    const host = createFakeHost({ folder });
    const result = await host.run(actions.saveNote, { kind: "text", text: "# Meeting notes\n\n- ship it" }, finder);
    assert.match(result.file, /\/Meeting notes\.md$/);
    assert.equal(new TextDecoder().decode(host.files.get(result.file)), "# Meeting notes\n\n- ship it\n");
  });

  test("namesTheFileSafely", () => {
    assert.equal(noteName("  \n Q3/Q4: plans \n", "Untitled note"), "Q3-Q4- plans.md");
    assert.equal(noteName("###", "Untitled note"), "Untitled note.md");
    assert.equal(noteName("x".repeat(100), "Untitled note"), `${"x".repeat(60)}.md`);
  });

  test("saysSoWhenThereIsNothingToSave", async () => {
    const host = createFakeHost({ folder });
    assert.deepEqual(await host.run(actions.saveNote, { kind: "text", text: "  " }, finder), { none: true, message: "There is no text to save." });
  });

  test("isOfferedOnlyForFinder", () => {
    const manifest = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(new URL("../manifest.json", import.meta.url), "utf8"));
    const [action] = manifest.contributes.actions;
    assert.deepEqual([action.targets, action.targetsOnly, action.output], [["finder"], true, "file"]);
  });
});
```

## Try it

```sh
npm test -- dev.yourname.save-note
npm run validate -- dev.yourname.save-note
npm run dev -- dev.yourname.save-note
```

Open a folder in Finder, copy some text in another app, then click the Finder window, press ⇧⌘V, select the text and press ⇧: *Save as Markdown note* leads the list, and ↵ drops the file into the folder.


================================================================================
File: docs/publishing.md
================================================================================

# Publishing

Extensions reach people through the store: this repository, a signed catalog built from it, and the Store tab in yabbistir's Settings → Extensions (coming in yabbistir 0.2.0). Publishing is a pull request.

## The flow

1. **Fork** this repository and make a branch.
2. **Write** the extension in `extensions/<id>/` (`npm run new -- <id> --template <template>`), with tests.
3. **Check** it: `npm test -- <id>`, `npm run validate -- <id>` and `npm run build -- <id>` pass, and you have tried it in the app with `npm run dev -- <id>`.
4. **Open a pull request.** The template asks what the extension does, for an example or a screenshot, for a reason for each permission, and for the tools it needs ([the template](../.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md)).
5. **Checks** run on the pull request (below). Fix what they report and push again.
6. **Review:** the maintainer reads the code against the [review checklist](review-checklist.md), and may ask for changes.
7. **Merge.** The maintainer squash-merges the pull request. Publishing then runs on `main`: every extension is built into a `.yabext` package, the catalog is generated with each package's SHA-256, signed with an Ed25519 key, and published to GitHub Pages ([how](#how-publishing-runs)).
8. **In the app,** the Store lists the new version the next time someone opens it or presses Refresh. Nothing is fetched in the background.

## What a pull request may change

- **One extension folder per pull request:** `extensions/<id>/` and nothing else, apart from the root `package-lock.json` when the extension adds a library, and the files `npm run docs` regenerates (the manifest reference quotes a real extension's manifest). A pull request that changes two extension folders, or other files next to its folder, fails the checks.
- Changes to the docs go in a pull request of their own, without an extension.
- **Only the maintainer changes** `.github/`, `tools/`, `packages/`, `templates/`, `schema/`, the root `package.json`, `package-lock.json` (beyond the libraries of the one extension a pull request changes) and `tsconfig.json`, and `.gitattributes` files: they decide what the workflows run, what npm installs and how every extension is built. A pull request that touches any of them fails the static checks. If something there should change, say so in your pull request or in an issue.
- **Someone else's extension:** fixes are welcome. A comment on the pull request names the extension's `author`, and mentions them when `author` is the GitHub login they committed the extension with, so they can weigh in; the maintainer decides.
- **Every change raises `version`** in manifest.json and adds a `## <version>` section to CHANGELOG.md, newest first.

## The checks

Each pull request runs, for the extension it changes:

- `npm run validate` and `npm run typecheck`.
- `npm run build`: Node modules and globals are caught here ([why](errors.md#node-builtins)).
- `npm test` for the extension, and the tools' own tests.
- Size: the `.yabext` at most 5 MB (5,000,000 bytes, the most the app downloads), `index.js` at most 1 MB.
- Readable source: a line over 500 characters, or a file whose lines average over 200 (blank lines aside), is taken for minified or obfuscated code and refused. This covers every file in `src/` and every file of the extension's folder that the build bundles, wherever it sits (`node_modules` aside). Write the source by hand, and let the build bundle libraries.
- Libraries from npm only: an extension's `package.json` is named after the extension (`"name": "<id>"`), names each library by its own name and a version, range or tag on the npm registry (no `npm:` alias, no git, `file:`, `link:` or URL dependency, no `bundleDependencies`), and has no `bin`, `scripts`, `directories` or `gypfile`; the folder has no `binding.gyp` and no committed `node_modules`. npm would otherwise fetch or run something no review saw. To add a library, write `extensions/<id>/package.json` as `{ "name": "<id>", "private": true }` (not with `npm init`, which adds `scripts`), then run `npm install <library>@<version> -w extensions/<id>` and commit both files.
- The lockfile, on every pull request that changes it: each changed entry is its own package's tarball on the npm registry (`https://registry.npmjs.org/<name>/-/<name>-<version>.tgz`, where `<name>` is the entry's own folder under `node_modules/`, so the address names the package and the version the entry claims) with a `sha512` integrity hash, or a workspace folder (`extensions/<id>` or `packages/<name>`, linked under its own package name). There are no aliases: an entry that installs one package under another's name is refused, and so is any `npm:` spec. Entries bundled inside another package (`inBundle`) are refused, since no address of their own can be checked, and so is a dependency spec that names a tarball file (`lib.tgz`). Beside an extension, only that extension's own libraries change: not the tools' packages or their platform builds, not another extension's, not one shared with them; and none has an install script or a command-line program. A lockfile change without an extension is the maintainer's (above); the checks still report whether each such change follows from a `package.json` change that asks for it. The tools' tests also compare `package-lock.json` with what `npm install --package-lock-only` writes.
- The license, a complete English locale, and regular files only: no symbolic links anywhere in the folder (from the validator).
- The install state of the whole repository (`tools/lockfile-state.mjs`): every entry of the lockfile, not only the changed ones, passes the rule above, and no two packages share an integrity hash; the root entry and each workspace entry ask for exactly the dependencies their `package.json` asks for, and each workspace `package.json` has its entry; there is no `npm-shrinkwrap.json` and no `.npmrc` at the root, which npm would read instead of, or on top of, the lockfile; the repository holds no symbolic link and no submodule anywhere, since a link can show a check one file and npm or the build another; no `node_modules` is committed anywhere under `extensions/`; and no two paths under `extensions/` differ only in letter case or Unicode normalization, which a Mac's disk would merge.
- `npm run docs` leaves no difference: a pull request that touches the docs, or what they are made from, commits what `npm run docs` writes.
- `npm run catalog` builds the store's catalog with the change, so a merge never stops publishing.

They run in two workflows:

- **Static checks** (`.github/workflows/static.yml`): the rules that only read files and git, which are what a pull request may change, the extensions' `package.json`, the lockfile and the install state. The workflow runs on `pull_request_target`, so GitHub takes it from the base branch, not from the pull request. It checks out three files of the base branch's last commit, the checker (`tools/static-checks.mjs`, `tools/lib/static-rules.mjs` and `tools/lockfile-state.mjs`), and the pull request's commits into a folder of their own; the checker reads the pull request's head commit through git (`git ls-tree`, `git cat-file`, `git diff`), never from the files on disk. It installs nothing, restores no cache, runs nothing of the pull request, and its token can read the repository and set commit statuses, nothing more. So a pull request cannot change what this check runs; the check is as good as the rules on `main`. It posts its result as the commit status `store/static-checks` on the pull request's head commit, success only when the checker passed, and branch protection on `main` requires that status ([what that rests on](#what-these-checks-do-not-cover)).
- **Checks** (`.github/workflows/pr.yml`): everything, the static rules included, with the pull request's own code: `npm ci --ignore-scripts` on macOS with Node 24 (npm 11), then build, validate, the tests, the docs and the catalog. The pull request can change this workflow and every file it runs, so its result is advisory: it shows a contributor what to fix and helps the review, and guarantees nothing.

Every check runs even when one fails, and the log ends with a list of them all. `npm run pr-checks` runs them all on your machine, on your checkout, for the commits since `origin/main` (add `-- --base <ref>` for another starting point); `node tools/static-checks.mjs` runs the static ones alone on your last commit, as the workflow does (`--base <ref>` and `--head <ref>` for others).

A pull request that changes `permissions`, `network` or `requires` (a tool's install command included), or adds an extension that asks for any of them, gets the `permissions-changed` label, so the review looks at it closely; so does one whose manifest the labelling cannot read. The workflow that labels reads the pull request through GitHub's API and never runs its code, and workflows that run on pull requests never see the signing key.

## Updates

An update is the same flow with a higher `version`. Installed copies update when the person chooses to, from the Store. An update that asks for a new permission, a new domain or a new tool waits until the person approves it. Never change the `id`: a new id is a new extension.

## The catalog

The app reads only static files, with no account, token or tracking:

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| Catalog | `https://berkaygkc.github.io/yabbistir-extensions/v1/catalog.json` |
| Its signature | `https://berkaygkc.github.io/yabbistir-extensions/v1/catalog.json.sig`: the base64 of a 64-byte Ed25519 signature over the catalog's exact bytes |
| Packages | `https://berkaygkc.github.io/yabbistir-extensions/v1/packages/<id>-<version>.yabext` |
| File icons | `https://berkaygkc.github.io/yabbistir-extensions/v1/icons/<id>.png`, for extensions with `icon.png` |
| Schemas | `https://berkaygkc.github.io/yabbistir-extensions/v1/catalog.schema.json` ([source](../schema/catalog.schema.json)) and `…/v1/manifest.schema.json` |

Each catalog entry has the extension's id, version, `apiVersion` and `minAppVersion`, its name and description in every language it ships, author, categories, icon, permissions, network hosts and tools, the package's SHA-256 and size, and the time of the last commit on `main` that changed the extension's folder (main's own commits, the merges: a branch's commits carry whatever date their author gave them). The same commit always gives the same catalog, byte for byte; `npm run catalog -- --out site/v1` writes it locally, unsigned. The app accepts a catalog only if its signature verifies with one of the keys built into the app, and installs a package only if its SHA-256 matches the catalog. An extension the app is too old for is listed but cannot be installed.

## How publishing runs

`.github/workflows/publish.yml` runs on every push to `main`, in three jobs:

1. **Build**, with no secret: first `node tools/lockfile-state.mjs` checks the install state of `main` as merged, on disk, with nothing installed, and stops the publish on any problem; then `npm ci --ignore-scripts` on Node 24, with no npm cache (none is restored, and `setup-node`'s automatic one is off), then `node tools/catalog.mjs --out site/v1` writes the catalog, the packages and the icons, unsigned. Node 24 brings npm 11: npm 10 still runs a git dependency's `prepare` script under `--ignore-scripts`. esbuild needs no install script: its platform build comes as an optional dependency.
2. **Sign**, in the `publish` environment, the only place the signing key exists. It checks out two paths, [`tools/sign.mjs`](../tools/sign.mjs) and `keys/catalog-public-keys.json`, and nothing else: no `package.json`, no `npm`, no `node_modules`. The signer uses Node's built-in modules only. Before it signs, it checks what it signs: format 1, every package under the `packages/` address above and next to the catalog with the size and SHA-256 the catalog states, every file icon under `icons/`, every readme on this repository, and nothing else in `site/` (only the catalog, the packages and icons it names, and the two schemas). Once the repository holds the app's public keys in `keys/catalog-public-keys.json` (`{ "keys": ["<base64 of a raw 32-byte key>", …] }`), it also refuses a signature none of them verifies, so a wrong secret never publishes a catalog every app rejects.
3. **Deploy** the signed `site/` to GitHub Pages, from the `github-pages` environment.

Signing and deploying run only for `main`.

### What these checks do not cover

- **The npm registry is trusted.** A library is what its author published under that name and version. The checks tie each lockfile entry to its own address on the registry and to a `sha512` hash, and npm checks each download against the hash; they cannot tell whether the published code is good. The review reads what an extension uses.
- **What only the maintainer changes relies on review alone.** A pull request that touches `.github/`, `tools/`, `packages/`, `templates/`, `schema/`, the root `package.json`, `package-lock.json` (beyond one extension's own libraries) or `tsconfig.json`, or a `.gitattributes`, fails the static checks; it is merged only when the maintainer has written or read it line by line and merges it past that failing check on purpose. Nothing automated judges such a change: a new version of a tool with everything it brings, a workflow edit, or an edit to the checker or to `tools/lockfile-state.mjs`, which every later pull request and publish then runs.
- **The checks job is advisory.** It runs the pull request's code, which can make it pass. The static checks, the install-state check before every publish, and the review are what keep a change from reaching the catalog unseen.
- **Publishing assumes a cold npm cache.** npm takes a package it has cached by its integrity hash alone, whatever address the lockfile names. The publish build restores no cache and turns off `setup-node`'s automatic one, and the install state lets one hash stand for one package only.
- **GitHub is trusted:** Actions and its runners, branch protection, `pull_request_target` running the base branch's workflow, the read-only token of workflows from forks, the environments that hold the signing key, and Pages.
- **The merge relies on branch protection.** `main` requires the commit status `store/static-checks`, on a branch that is up to date with `main`. Only a token that may write commit statuses can set it: the static workflow's, which runs from the base branch, or the maintainer's own. A workflow that a pull request from a fork adds runs with a read-only token, so it cannot set that status, even if it names a job "Static checks".

## The .yabext package

`npm run build -- <id>` writes `dist/<id>-<version>.yabext`: a zip whose root is a folder named after the id.

```text
<id>/manifest.json
<id>/index.js
<id>/locales/en.json
<id>/locales/tr.json
<id>/README.md
<id>/CHANGELOG.md
<id>/icon.png           only with a file icon
```

The archive is deterministic: entries in sorted order, every date set to 1980-01-01, fixed permissions, so the same source always gives the same bytes and the same SHA-256. The source (`src/`, `tests/`) is not in it.

To try a package without the store, install it in yabbistir: Settings → Extensions → Development → Install .yabext… (or Install from Folder… with `dist/<id>`). The app asks for the permissions first, and marks it as not signed.


================================================================================
File: docs/review-checklist.md
================================================================================

# Review checklist

Every pull request is read against this list before it is merged. Authors: go through it before you open one, and say in the pull request how each point that applies is met. The automated checks ([Publishing](publishing.md#the-checks)) cover what a machine can see. This list is for what takes a person.

## Data

- [ ] Nothing about the person leaves the Mac except what the action is for, and only when the person runs it. No analytics, no telemetry, no "phone home", no tracking parameters added to requests.
- [ ] The item's content goes only to the host the action is about, and the README says so.
- [ ] `console.log` and thrown messages never contain the item's content, a secret or a token; the Development log is still a log.
- [ ] Secrets are read with `yab.secrets.get` only where needed, never logged, never put in a result, never sent anywhere but their own service.
- [ ] `yab.storage` holds settings or small caches, not copies of the person's clipboard.
- [ ] Files are written only in the work folder; a `folder` preference is only read.

## Permissions

- [ ] Each permission has a reason in the pull request and in the README, and the extension cannot do its job without it.
- [ ] `network` lists the hosts it needs. An empty list (any host) needs a strong reason, such as an action whose whole point is any link.
- [ ] `capture` only for extensions whose purpose is a capture rule. A rule is fast, pure and keeps the copy when unsure.
- [ ] `history` only when the action is about earlier copies.
- [ ] On-device features (`yab.ai`, `yab.translate`) are preferred over a web service when they can do the job.

## exec

- [ ] Each tool in `requires.tools` is needed, named by its bare command, with an `install` command that works (`brew install …`).
- [ ] **Arguments are fixed or checked by the extension.** Anything that comes from the item (a link, a file name, text) is one argument, after `--` when the tool accepts it, so it can never be read as an option.
- [ ] No option that runs another program, reads a config file from elsewhere or writes outside the work folder (for yt-dlp: no `--exec`, `--config-locations`, `--batch-file`, `--netrc`), unless the reason is in the pull request.
- [ ] No shell (`sh`, `bash`, `zsh`, `osascript`) as a tool.
- [ ] The exit code is checked; output is parsed, not trusted.
- [ ] Cancelling stops the tool: `ctx.signal` is passed to `yab.exec`.

## Download Video and browser cookies

- [ ] The browser-cookies preference is **off by default** and asks for confirmation (`confirm`) when turned on.
- [ ] Cookies are handed **only to yt-dlp**, by naming the browser (`--cookies-from-browser <browser>`). The extension never reads, logs, stores or sends them anywhere else.
- [ ] The confirmation text and the README say so plainly, and say that Safari needs Full Disk Access.
- [ ] YouTube needs `deno` for yt-dlp's challenges; it is listed in `requires.tools`.

## Behaviour

- [ ] Expected situations return `{ none: true, message }`; thrown errors are real failures with a message a person can act on.
- [ ] `cancelled` errors are let through, never swallowed.
- [ ] Hints, detectors, previews and rules have no effects and stay well inside their time limits.
- [ ] `accepts` is as narrow as it can be: the action appears only where it can help.
- [ ] Jobs report progress calmly (state words, whole percents) and have a `failTitle`.

## Naming and words

- [ ] Names, titles, subtitles, tags and messages follow the [design guidelines](design-guidelines.md#naming): short, plain, sentence-case actions starting with a verb.
- [ ] `locales/en.json` is complete and reads naturally. Other languages are welcome.
- [ ] Keywords are what people would type.

## Design

- [ ] The extension leaves drawing to the app: no attempts at color, emoji decoration, ASCII art or HTML used as a layout.
- [ ] The icon is an SF Symbol (`sf:…`), or an `icon.png` that is a simple grey glyph that reads in light and dark mode, without brand colors ([Icons](design-guidelines.md#icons)).
- [ ] Preview sections are few and plain.

## Code and package

- [ ] The source is readable and written by hand. Libraries, if any, are in the extension's own `package.json` at exact versions, and are plain JavaScript.
- [ ] No Node modules or globals (the build checks), no `eval` or `new Function`, no code fetched at run time.
- [ ] Tests cover the main path, the messages, and the expected failures.
- [ ] README: what it does, an example, every permission with its reason, the tools to install. CHANGELOG has the new version.
- [ ] The license is MIT or another the store accepts, and any bundled library's license allows it.
- [ ] The pull request changes one extension folder and raises its version.

## Checklist

- [ ] `npm test -- <id>`, `npm run validate -- <id>`, `npm run build -- <id>` and `npm run typecheck` pass.
- [ ] I tried it in yabbistir with `npm run dev -- <id>`.
- [ ] Only `extensions/<id>/` changed, and its `version` is raised for a change.
- [ ] README.md explains what it does and every permission; CHANGELOG.md has this version.
- [ ] I went through [the review checklist](https://github.com/berkaygkc/yabbistir-extensions/blob/main/docs/review-checklist.md).
